baseline.patient_history: Per Colorectal Surgery Consult Note: ___ with prior traumatic splenectomy presents to the ED with ~20 hours of abdominal cramping. The patient had a routine screening colonoscopy performed yesterday late morning. His stool was clear prior to the scope, see detailed report below of what was described as an easy to complete, routine colonoscopy, no polypectomies required, evidence of some mild sigmoid diverticulosis. After the procedure, he experienced persistent abdominal cramping, bloating, and failure to pass flatus or stool. He feels like the pain is mainly focused in the RLQ. Mild nausea, no vomiting, fever to 102 with chills and sweats. Has not eaten anything since the procedure. Has been urinating normally. Patient also describes a recent tick bite on his left lateral thigh, spending a lot of time in ___. He noticed it about a week and a half ago, pulled it off, and at that point it had been ___ days since he had last been in ___. He was treated for Lyme in the past, unsure if he actually had the true diagnosis. Has not yet been tested. Additionally, he has a healing "bump" on his left buttock just lateral to the gluteal cleft that felt like a boil and has been healing, but was a bit sore for awhile. Has not drained pus. Had not had fevers until overnight. Past Medical History: none Social History: Married, supportive wife

EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis after the administration of 150 cc of intravenous Visipaque. Axial
images were interpreted in conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.
Oral contrast was not administered.

DLP:
1122.3 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
Limited assessment of the lung bases demonstrates bilateral, right
greater than left, lower lobes atelectasis. No pleural effusion. The
visualized heart is normal in size without pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is homogeneous in enhancement. No focal lesion identified.No
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. The gallbladder is normal
without calcified gallstones. The portal vein, SMV, and splenic vein are
patent.

The spleen is normal. 1.7 x 1.2 and 0.7 x 0.7 cm accessory spleens are noted
(02:11). The pancreas enhances homogenously and is without focal lesions,
peripancreatic fat stranding, or focal fluid collection. The adrenal glands
are unremarkable.

The kidneys display symmetric nephrograms and excretion of contrast.  No focal
renal lesions. No hydronephrosis or hydroureter identified.  No renal or
proximal ureter calculi.

The distal esophagus is normal without hiatal hernia. The stomach is grossly
unremarkable in appearance. The small bowel is top normal in the caliber and
appears stacked without wall thickening likely representing an ileus. Mild fat
stranding and wall thickening is seen along the ascending colon predominately
along the cecum with thickening of the right lateroconal fascia. The remaining
large bowel is normal in caliber without wall thickening, fat stranding, or
focal mass lesion.

A 0.5 x 0.5 cm (601b:36) appendicolith is seen at the base of the appendix.
The appendix is hyperemic and air-filled measuring 1 cm in maximal diameter.
Adjacent to the proximal portion of the appendix there is extraluminal free
air. A 2.5 x 1.2 cm (601b:36) collection which is predominately full of air is
seen slightly anterior to the appendix. An additional 5.7 x 2.6 cm (2:63) air
and fluid filled collection is seen slightly superior to the appendix and may
be in continuation with the previously identified collection. Secondary
inflammation of the base of the cecum and ascending colon is present. The
terminal ileum is within normal limits. Mild fat stranding is seen along the
distal ileum with a 3.3 x 3.4 cm and 2.4 x 1.8 cm (601b:30) pockets of fluid
within the mesenteric leaves.

The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber without aneurysmal dilatation. The
celiac axis, SMA, and ___ are patent .  The iliac arteries are normal in
course and caliber.

No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node enlargement by CT size criteria.
No abdominal wall hernia.

PELVIS:
The bladder is well distended and normal. No pelvic side-wall or
inguinal lymph node enlargement by CT size criteria. Small amount of free
pelvic fluid seen. The prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No focal lytic or sclerotic lesion concerning for
malignancy.

TECHNIQUE:
___ MDCT-acquired axial images from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis were displayed with 5-mm slice thickness.  Intravenous contrast was
administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The lung bases are clear.  No focal
pulmonary nodule or mass is identified.  There is no pleural effusion.  The
imaged cardiac apex is within normal limits.

The liver demonstrates homogeneous parenchymal enhancement without suspicious
focal lesion.  The hepatic veins and portal venous system are grossly patent. 
No intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation is identified.  The
gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands are normal.  There is
symmetric enhancement and excretion of both kidneys without suspicious focal
lesion or hydronephrosis.  The abdominal aorta and its branch vessels are
non-aneurysmal and grossly patent.  There is no abdominal free fluid or free
air.  The stomach and small bowel loops are normal in caliber and
configuration without evidence of obstruction or inflammation.  The appendix
is prominent measuring up to 6 mm in maximum diameter.  The tip is ill-defined
and has some mild surrounding fat stranding and fascial thickening.  Findings
are equivocal for early acute tip ____.

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The rectum and colon are normal in
caliber and configuration without evidence of obstruction or inflammation. 
There is a moderate amount of stool within the cecum and ascending colon.  The
uterus and adnexa appear within normal limits on this CT examination.  No
large adnexal mass lesion is identified.  There is no appreciable pelvic free
fluid. The bladder is moderately distended and appears normal.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No bone destructive lesion or acute fracture is
identified.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique. IV Contrast:  130 mL Omnipaque.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.
Oral contrast was not administered.

DOSE:
This study involved 5 CT acquisition phases with dose indices as
follows:
   1) CT Localizer Radiograph
   2) CT Localizer Radiograph
   3) Stationary Acquisition 0.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 4.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 2.4
mGy-cm.
   4) Stationary Acquisition 3.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 28.9 mGy (Body) DLP =
14.4 mGy-cm.
   5) Spiral Acquisition 4.7 s, 51.5 cm; CTDIvol = 16.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 866.5
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 883 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
There is bibasilar atelectasis.  No pleural or pericardial
effusion.

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
There is a 1.5 x 1.4 cm intermediate density nodule in the left
adrenal gland.  The right adrenal gland is unremarkable.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  There are dilated fluid-filled
proximal small bowel loops measuring up to 5 cm with a gradual transition with
distal loops of small bowel more decompressed.  Mid to distal small bowel
loops demonstrate wall thickening and surrounding stranding.  The colon is
largely decompressed.  The appendix is thick walled and dilated measuring up
to 13 mm with a 13 mm appendicolith within the appendiceal base.  There is a 2
x 1.7 x 3.8 cm collection of fluid with foci of air within it located medial
to the appendix (601b:37 and 02:43).  There is a small amount of ascites
within the abdomen and tracking into the pelvis.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  Some free
fluid is demonstrated in the left lower quadrant.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The uterus is massively enlarged with numerous intramural
fibroids as well as multiple pedunculated sub serosal fibroids the largest of
which is located on the left measuring 8.6 x 9.3 x 8.3 cm.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES:
A 1.9 x 3.9 cm fluid density ovoid structure just to the right
and superior to the umbilicus in the anterior abdominal wall may reflect a
cyst or fluid containing hernia.

in person on ___ at 09:30 AM, 30 minutes after discovery of the
findings.

EXAMINATION:
CT abdomen and pelvis

TECHNIQUE:
Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Total DLP (Body) = 499 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
Imaged lung bases are clear.

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  Main portal vein is patent.  Mild
periportal edema likely reflects aggressive hydration.  There is no
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within
normal limits.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas appears normal.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach and duodenum appear normal.  Small bowel loops
demonstrate no signs of ileus, obstruction, or wall thickening.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  In the right lower abdomen, the appendix is
dilated to 16 mm in diameter, with mucosal hyperemia.  Two large
appendicoliths measure 13 and 15 mm, one lodged at the base of the appendix
(2:42, 2:44), and the second within the proximal lumen.  There is
periappendiceal fat stranding, a significant volume of free fluid without
discrete drainable fluid collection.  The wall of the appendix appears
discontinuous raising concern for perforation (601:24, 02:43).  There is no
free air.  No CT signs of peritonitis.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The prostate and seminal vesicles are normal.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
No evidence of thrombophlebitis region inflammation the right
abdomen.  There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

NOTIFICATION:
The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by ___,
M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 6:00 pm, immediately after discovery of
the findings.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis before and after the administration of IV contrast only per the
mesenteric CTA protocol.  Sagittal and coronal reformatted images were
obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
There is bibasilar atelectasis.  No focal consolidations or
nodules are identified.  There is no pleural effusion.  The base of the heart
is normal in size.  Mild atherosclerotic calcifications are noted along the
coronary arteries.  There is no pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is normal in shape and contour.  On the arterial phase, in
the dome of the liver, there is a small 7-mm enhancing focus isoattenuating on
later phase most consistent with a transient hepatic perfusion anomaly.  No
other focal hepatic lesions are identified.  There is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary duct dilation.  The portal vein is patent.  The hepatic
artery is normal.  The gallbladder is mildly distended with multiple stones. 
This is no CT evidence of cholecystitis.  The spleen, pancreas, and left
adrenal gland are normal.  In the right adrenal gland, there is a 26 x 26 mm
hypodense lesion, consistent with an adrenal adenoma.  The kidneys are normal
without focal renal lesions.  There is no evidence of pyelonephritis or
hydronephrosis.  The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically.  The
stomach and small bowel are normal in course and caliber.  There is no
evidence of obstruction.  There are no focal inflammatory changes.  There is
no free air or free fluid.  The SMA and the mesenteric branches are patent
without evidence of an embolus.  The ___ is patent.  There is moderate
atherosclerotic disease along the course of the abdominal aorta which is
mildly ectatic, up to 2.4 cm below the renal arteries.  The bilateral common
iliac arteries are ectatic, slightly more on the right than the left.  The
right measures up to 1.7 cm (4A, 123); the left measures up to 1.4 cm (4A,
112).  There are moderate atherosclerotic calcifications along their course. 
There is no mesenteric, abdominal, or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  In the
left paraortic space just below the left renal artery, there is a nonenhancing
15 x 17 mm cystic structure, which may represent a lymphangioma.

PELVIS:
The appendix is abnormal.  It is thickened at its base with dilation
of the middle portion up to 17 mm (4A, 113).  There is an air-fluid level
within the appendix.  The tip is normal.  There is mild surrounding stranding.
There is a large fecal load in the cecum and ascending colon.  The large bowel
is otherwise normal without focal inflammatory changes.

The bladder is unremarkable.  The prostate is mildly enlarged measuring up to
5.2 cm.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free
fluid in the pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There are no concerning lytic or sclerotic osseous
lesions.  No fracture is identified.  Moderate degenerative changes are noted
in the lower lumber spine.

TECHNIQUE:
CT of the chest was obtained after the administration of IV
contrast.  Coronal, sagittal and maximum intensity oblique plane re-formatted
images were reviewed.

FINDINGS:
There is no evidence of pulmonary arterial filling defect is subsegmental
level.  The aorta and great vessels are unremarkable aside from minimal
atherosclerotic calcification.  The heart is normal in size with minimal
coronary artery calcification.  There is no pericardial effusion.

A top normal right lower paratracheal node (10 mm, 2:34) is likely reactive. 
There is no mediastinal lymphadenopathy.  Similarly, a right hilar node
measures up to 1.4 cm (2:45).

A 7 mm nodule left upper lobe appears to have long pleural tail suggestive of
this being a focal benign area, perhaps mucous plugging rather than worrisome
nodule, however malignancy cannot be excluded and can have a similar
appearance.  Elsewhere, there is segmental and subsegmental atelectasis as
well as airway thickening and air bronchograms.  There is no evidence of
infection.  There is no pleural effusion.

Below the diaphragm, ascites is again noted. A tiny sub centimeter hyperdense
focus in the dome of the liver is likely clinically inconsequential. There are
no suspicious bony lesions.

FINDINGS:
Four frontal and upright views of the abdomen demonstrate multiple dilated
loops of small and large bowel with numerous air-fluid levels within the small
bowel.  There is no definite air seen in the rectum.  There is no pneumatosis
or free air.  The visualized osseous structures demonstrate moderate
degenerative changes of the lumbar spine.  There are bilateral small pleural
effusions.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
after the administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque intravenous contrast. 
Sagittal and coronal reformations were performed and reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The imaged lung bases and heart are
unremarkable.  There is a small hiatal hernia.

The liver enhances homogeneously without focal lesions.  The gallbladder,
adrenal glands, spleen, and pancreas are normal.  Both kidneys enhance and
excrete contrast symmetrically, without hydronephrosis or renal masses.  The
stomach and small bowel loops are normal.  The appendix is fluid filled and
dilated measuring 13 mm, with extensive periappendiceal fat stranding,
consistent with ____.  No evidence of perforation is seen. 
There is mild secondary inflammation of the adjacent terminal ileum. The
abdominal aorta is normal in course and caliber.  No significant
retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy is seen.

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The urinary bladder is partially filled
with a Foley catheter in place.  The rectum and sigmoid colon are normal.  The
uterus is enlarged measuring 13.5 x 9.2 cm, with a large hypo-enhancing lesion
measuring 7.8 x 5.0 cm (2:62).  This likely represents a degenerating fibroid.
No adnexal abnormalities are seen. Small amount of pelvic free fluid is seen.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
No bone lesions suspicious for infection or
malignancy are detected.

FINDINGS:
AP upright and supine views of the abdomen and pelvis show mildly
distended loops of small bowel with multiple air-fluid levels and a string of
pearls sign in the loops on the right.  There is paucity of gas within the
colon.  The constellation of these findings is suggestive of a small bowel
obstruction; however, taking into account patient's postoperative history,
adynamic ileus is also a possiblity.  No pneumatosis and no intra-abdominal
free air.  Surgical staples are noted over the midline.  Osseous structures
show degenerative changes.

hyperdensity is consistent with an appendicolith (601B:20).  At this level,

compatible with secondary inflammation.

adrenal glands and kidneys appear grossly unremarkable.  Loops of small and
large bowel are normal in size and caliber.

The bladder, distal ureters and uterus appear grossly unremarkable.

No free air or lymphadenopathy is seen.

No concerning osseous lesion is seen.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
PELVIC ULTRASOUND:
Transabdominal and transvaginal examination was performed,
the latter to further evaluate the endometrium and adnexal structures.  The
uterus measures 6.2 x 3.2 x 3.6 cm.  An intrauterine device grossly appears
within standard position within the fundal endometrium.  The ovaries are
normal demonstrating normal arterial and venous Doppler waveforms.  There is
no evidence of ovarian torsion.  There is a small amount of free fluid within
the pelvis. Targeted ultrasound examination was then performed in the right
lower quadrant at the site of patient's pain.  There is a tubular structure at
this site measuring 5 mm in diameter.  On realtime scanning, compression of
the structure could not be verified.  However, no hyperemia was seen and a
blind end could not be confirmed.  Findings may represent a dilated appendix,
though sonographic findings are inconclusive.  CT of the abdomen and pelvis is
recommended for further characterization.

Total DLP (Body) = 537 mGy-cm.

There is mild dependent atelectasis bilaterally. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.

which is incompletely characterized.  It is in close proximity to both portal
venous and hepatic venous branches.  There is no evidence of other focal
lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen measures 13.3 cm.  It shows normal attenuation throughout,
without evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  Dilated, fluid-filled, hyperemic presacral
appendix measures 11 mm with hyperemic mucosa.

The prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.

There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or
acute fracture.  The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN):

TECHNIQUE:
Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:


LIVER:
The liver is diffusely echogenic.  The contour of the liver is smooth. 
A simple appearing hepatic cyst is seen in the right hepatic lobe measuring
4.5 x 4 x 3.9 cm.  There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is
patent with hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS:
There is mild intrahepatic biliary dilation.

CBD:
Two stones are seen in the proximal CBD, measuring 1.5 and 1 cm
respectively, and the CBD itself appears dilated measuring up to 15 mm.

GALLBLADDER:
The gallbladder is markedly abnormal.  The gallbladder wall is
irregular, thickened and edematous and appears decompressed.  There is a focal
defect in the anterior aspect of the wall which connects to a heterogeneous
fluid collection medially along the undersurface of the liver.  This
collection measures approximately 3.0 x 1.8 cm.  There is mild pericholecystic
edema.

PANCREAS:
The head and body of the pancreas are within normal limits. The tail
of the pancreas is not visualized due to the presence of gas.

SPLEEN:
Normal echogenicity.
  Spleen length: 10.7 cm

KIDNEYS:
Limited views of the kidneys show no hydronephrosis.
  Right kidney: 11.1 cm

RETROPERITONEUM:
The visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
with intravenous contrast administration.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.4 s, 58.7 cm; CTDIvol = 24.3 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,427.6 mGy-cm.
   2) Stationary Acquisition 0.6 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 3.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 1.7
mGy-cm.
   3) Stationary Acquisition 6.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 33.5 mGy (Body) DLP =
16.8 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,446 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
Lungs: Small bilateral pleural effusions are seen, slightly greater on the
right, with associated subsegmental atelectasis.

Pleural calcifications are seen, suggesting previous asbestos exposure.

A 1.0 cm subcutaneous nodule is partially visualized in the anterior chest
wall, series 2, image 1, which could represent a sebaceous cyst.

The distal tip of a pacemaker lead is partially visualized.

Liver: The liver is homogeneous with a smooth contour. A few subcentimeter
lesions are seen scattered throughout the liver, for example in segment 2,
series 2, image 22, too small to characterize, but likely cysts or biliary
hamartomas.  No suspicious liver lesion.

Biliary: There is no intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile duct dilatation. There
is mild distention of the gallbladder with extensive pericholecystic stranding
and fluid.  There is mucosal irregularity, with areas of hyperenhancement and
lack of enhancement, and probable perforation anteriorly.  No gas is seen.

No radiopaque stones are seen.

Spleen: The spleen is not enlarged and is homogeneous.

Pancreas: Unremarkable. There is no pancreatic duct dilatation.

Adrenal glands: Unremarkable.

Urinary: There is moderate to severe bilateral hydroureter and hydronephrosis.
The ureters are medially displaced and markedly tortuous.  There is atrophy
and areas of cortical scarring of the left kidney.

Pelvis: The urinary bladder is collapsed and contains a Foley catheter in the
small amount of air. The wall appears thickened, likely sequelae of chronic
outlet obstruction.

There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

There is marked prostatomegaly.

Gastrointestinal: Colonic diverticula are seen. There is mild wall thickening
of the second and third part of the duodenum, likely reactive due to adjacent
gallbladder inflammation.  There is no evidence of bowel dilatation or
obstruction.

Vascular: There are moderate atherosclerotic calcifications of the abdominal
aorta.  Early takeoff of the right hepatic artery from the celiac trunk.

The portal vein and hepatic veins are patent.

Lymph nodes: There is no size significant lymph nodes.

Bone and soft tissues: There is no suspicious bone lesion.  Moderate
degenerative disc disease is seen in the lumbar spine. A small left
fat-containing inguinal hernia is seen.

EXAMINATION:
LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN):

TECHNIQUE:
Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:


LIVER:
The liver is diffusely echogenic. The contour of the liver is smooth.
There is no focal liver mass. The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal
flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS:
There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER:
Cholelithiasis in the gallbladder fundus without gallbladder wall
thickening.

PANCREAS:
Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

KIDNEYS:
Limited views of bilateral kidneys demonstrate normal cortical
echogenicity and cortical medullary differentiation bilaterally without
evidence of masses, stones, or hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM:
Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial multidetector CT images were obtained through the torso
after the uneventful administration of intravenous contrast in the arterial
phase.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal images through the chest, abdomen,
and pelvis, and oblique maximal intensity projection images of the chest were
submitted to PACS and reviewed.

DOSE:
Total DLP (Body) = 534 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:


HEART AND VASCULATURE:
Pulmonary vasculature is well opacified to the
subsegmental level without filling defect to indicate a pulmonary embolus. 
The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber without evidence of intraluminal
dissection or intramural hematoma.  Mixed density soft tissue thickening in
the posterior mediastinum including multiple discrete-appearing foci of
hyperdensity, some of which are partially calcified and reniform in shape are
most consistent with calcified mediastinal lymph nodes.

PLEURAL SPACES:
A moderate to large high density left pleural effusion is
noted.
LUNGS/AIRWAYS:  Subsegmental atelectasis is noted in bilateral lung bases. 
Mild interlobular septal thickening suggests volume overload.  The airways are
patent to the level of the subsegmental bronchi bilaterally.  Innumerable
pulmonary nodules are seen bilaterally measuring up to 8 mm, for which
followup chest CT in 3 months is recommended to evaluate for stability (3:70,
81, 87, 91, 130, 134, 143, 148, 155, 156, 158, 160, 164, 167, 175, 191).

BASE OF NECK:
Visualized portions of the base of the neck show no abnormality.

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
Hyperemia of the hepatic parenchyma adjacent to the gallbladder
fossa is noted with a punctate gallstone seen dependently within the
gallbladder fundus (2:134).  The gallbladder is mildly distended but without
pericholecystic fluid or gallbladder wall edema.  There is no evidence of
focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation. There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis. There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized.  There is no
free intraperitoneal fluid or free air.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or
acute fracture.  Irregularity of the posterior right ninth and tenth ribs is
likely due to remote prior fracture.  The abdominal and pelvic wall is within
normal limits.

findings.

free fluid.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

EXAMINATION:
CT abdomen pelvis with IV contrast.

SBO:


TECHNIQUE:
Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were
acquired through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast
administration with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 3.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 14.4 mGy (Body) DLP =
7.2 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.2 s, 49.1 cm; CTDIvol = 23.6 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,155.6 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,163 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
Visualized lung fields are within normal limits. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
Geographic hypodensity adjacent to the falciform ligament
likely represents focal fatty deposition.  Otherwise, the liver demonstrates
homogenous enhancement.  No focal liver lesions.  No intra or extrahepatic
biliary dilatation.  There is circumferential gallbladder wall
edema/pericholecystic fluid, which is concerning for ____. 
Punctate gallstones are seen layering dependently (series 601 image 26). 
There is also a punctate stone at the gallbladder neck (series 2, image 26). 
10 mm hyperenhancing focus at the gallbladder fundus may represent focal
adenomyomatosis (series 2, image 36, series 602, image 30).  An additional 1.4
cm hyperenhancing focus near the gallbladder neck (series 601, image 27) is
likely a reactive lymph node.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
Subcentimeter hypodensity within the lower pole the right kidney is
too small to characterize, but likely represents a simple cyst.  Otherwise,
the kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram.  There is
no evidence of hydronephrosis.  There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
Small hiatal hernia.  The stomach is unremarkable.  Small
bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement
throughout.  The colon and rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is
normal.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The patient is status post hysterectomy.  No adnexal
masses are visualized.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

The visualized lung bases are clear with no pleural effusions,

The liver enhances homogeneously with no focal lesions. The portal and
hepatic veins are patent, and there is no intra or extrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation.

The gallbladder is distended with multiple gallstones and a
gallstone at the gallbladder neck (02:29). The gallbladder wall is thickened
with mucosal hyperemia and adjacent fat stranding.

The spleen is normal in size and shape.

A 7 mm pancreatic tail cyst is smaller compared to ___
when it measured 1.1 x 1.2 cm (2:31). There is no pancreatic ductal dilation.

The adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

The kidneys are normal in size and shape.  Renal hypodensities are
compatible with cysts, previously characterized on prior MR from ___. The kidneys have appropriate contrast enhancement and excretion
bilaterally.  There is hydronephrosis or perinephric stranding.

Small hiatal hernia is present. The stomach is mildly distended and
unremarkable.  There is wall edema within the duodenum adjacent to the
inflamed gallbladder (2:38), likely reactive. The remaining small bowel is
without obstruction or focal wall thickening.  The appendix is not visualized,
but there are no secondary findings to suggest appendicitis. The large bowel
contains feces without wall thickening or evidence of obstruction.  Suture
material likely representing prior colonic resection and anastomosis is noted
at the hepatic flexure (2:40). There is no intraperitoneal free air or free
fluid.

There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

The bladder is relatively well distended without focal wall
thickening. There is no pelvic free fluid. There are no pathologically

inguinal surgical clip is seen (2:79). The rectum is unremarkable.

are patent.

malignancy. Degenerative changes within the thoracolumbar spine are noted
along with scoliosis.

Minimal atelectasis is identified at
the lung bases.  The imaged cardiac apex is within normal limits.

The liver demonstrates homogeneous parenchymal enhancement without discrete
lesion.  The hepatic veins and portal venous system are grossly patent.  The
patient is status post recent ERCP with biliary stent placement in the common
bile duct.  The stent appears in expected position with extension of the
proximal limb into the left intrahepatic duct.  A tiny focus of central
pneumobilia is likely related to recent procedure (5:18).  Mild prominence of
the central intrahepatic ducts remains.  The gallbladder is markedly distended
and has surrounding stranding/fluid and wall edema.  In the setting of
abdominal pain and leukocytosis, ____ is within the
differential, however, followup ultrasound is recommended.  The spleen and
adrenal glands appear within normal limits.  The pancreatic parenchyma appears
normal.  There is mild prominence of the pancreatic duct throughout its
course, unchanged compared to prior examination.  This could be evaluated by
___ non-emergently if clinically indicated.  There is symmetric enhancement
of the kidneys without suspicious focal lesion or hydronephrosis.  Numerous
subcentimeter hypodensities within both kidneys remain too small to
characterize, though likely represent small cysts.  Abdominal aorta and branch
vessels demonstrate severe atherosclerotic calcifications, though are
non-aneurysmal and grossly patent.  Bi-iliac stent grafts are in expected
position and are patent.  

The patient is status post recent ___ fundoplication secondary to a hiatal
hernia.  Post-surgical changes near the gastroesophageal junction appear
within normal limits.  No recurrent hiatal hernia is evident.  Small bowel is

is identified.

and configuration without evidence of obstruction or inflammation.  The
bladder contains a Foley catheter and a small amount of air.  Uterus and
adnexa are unremarkable.  No pelvic fluid is identified.

are likely secondary to recent injections.  Post-surgical appearance of the
thoracolumbar spine is overall unchanged in compared to prior examination.  No
acute fracture or bone destructive lesion is identified.

opacities most likely represent atelectasis and chronic lung changes.  No
definite focal consolidation is seen.  There is no pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.  The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are unremarkable.

CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast

Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique. Oral contrast was administered.Coronal and
sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

Total DLP (Body) = 928 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
Atelectasis seen in the lung bases.  Atherosclerotic
calcifications are noted in the coronary arteries.  There is no evidence of
pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. There
is a trace amount of perihepatic ascites. There is no evidence of focal
lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is distended and contains cholelithiasis with
mild pericholecystic fluid.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
A large simple cyst in the interpolar region of the left kidney measuring 7.2
x 8.6 cm.  There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis. 
There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Mild sigmoid
diverticulosis is noted without evidence of acute diverticulitis.  Otherwise,
the colon and rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is normal.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The uterus is resected.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Moderate atherosclerotic
disease is noted.

BONES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Degenerative changes are seen in the visualized spine.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.  There
are small bilateral fat containing inguinal hernias.

discussion with attending radiologist.

was placed on the fluoroscopy table. A time-out confirming the patient's

performed. We attempted to place the patient prone, but this was not possible
due to patient discomfort. We next placed the patient in a semi-decubitus
position and a preprocedural scout film was obtained. An appropriate
fluoroscopic target was unable to be obtained, despite additional attempts at
changing patient position. The procedure was aborted.

Unable to attempt lumbar puncture due to inability to position patient and
obtain an adequate fluoroscopic target.

contrast material. Subsequently, rapid axial imaging was performed through the
brain during infusion of intravenous contrast material. Images were processed
on a separate workstation with display 3D volume rendered images, and maximum
intensity projection images.

DLP: 699.25 mGy-cm; CTDI:  57.31 mGy

right frontal lobe encephalomalacia and postoperative findings compatible with
reported history of right AVM resection. There is associated streak artifact

acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect.  The ventricles are prominent in

intracranial vasculature. Atheromatous catheterization vascular calcifications

at both femoral acetabular joints with prominent acetabular spurring.

EXAMINATION:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH:

TECHNIQUE:
Chest, AP upright and lateral views.

FINDINGS:
The lung volumes are low.  There is moderate relative elevation of the right
hemidiaphragm compared to the left.  The heart appears normal in size.  There
is perhaps very mild perihilar congestion bilaterally.  Elsewhere, the lungs
appear clear.  There are no pleural effusions or pneumothorax.

EXAMINATION:
Head CT.

TECHNIQUE:
Non-contrast CT.

DOSE:
402.4 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
There has been no significant change.  There is again a large area of
encephalomalacia within the frontal lobe with surrounding clips and metallic
artifact which to some extent limits evaluation. A small extra-axial
collection of low density is unchanged and probably post-operative, underlying
a right frontal craniotomy site.  Ventricles appear stable in configuration.
There is no evidence for intracranial hemorrhage or acute process.  Cavernous
carotid artery calcifications are extensive.  There is been prior left
mastoidectomy with placement of a cochlear implant whose hardware overlies the
left parietal skull, also generating metallic artifact which obscures portions
of the brain.  Otherwise soft tissue structures are unremarkable. There is
minimal ethmoid sinus mucosal thickening.  No fracture is identified.

EXAMINATION:
LUMBAR PUNCTURE (W/ FLUORO):

TECHNIQUE:
Consent was obtained from the patient's primary team. The patient
was placed on the fluoroscopy table. A time-out confirming the patient's
identity, procedure to be performed, and relevant clinical history was
performed. We attempted to place the patient prone, but this was not possible
due to patient discomfort. We next placed the patient in a semi-decubitus
position and a preprocedural scout film was obtained. An appropriate
fluoroscopic target was unable to be obtained, despite additional attempts at
changing patient position. The procedure was aborted.

FINDINGS:
Unable to attempt lumbar puncture due to inability to position patient and
obtain an adequate fluoroscopic target.

NOTIFICATION:
Termination of procedure was discussed by Dr. ___ Dr.
___ neurology at 12:30 ___.

EXAMINATION:
CTA HEAD WANDW/O C AND RECONS:

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without
contrast material. Subsequently, rapid axial imaging was performed through the
brain during infusion of intravenous contrast material. Images were processed
on a separate workstation with display 3D volume rendered images, and maximum
intensity projection images.

DOSE:
DLP: 699.25 mGy-cm; CTDI:  57.31 mGy

FINDINGS:
Head CT:  There postoperative changes of a prior right frontal craniotomy with
right frontal lobe encephalomalacia and postoperative findings compatible with
reported history of right AVM resection. There is associated streak artifact
over the right frontal lobe which obscures evaluation. There is no evidence of
acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect.  The ventricles are prominent in
size though unchanged when compared to prior exams. Left mastoidectomy with
left-sided cochlear implant produces additional streak artifact.

Head an CTA:  There is a large amount of embolization material within the
right frontal lobe compatible with a history of prior AVM embolization. There
is no evidence of aneurysm or pathologic large vessel occlusion within the
intracranial vasculature. Atheromatous catheterization vascular calcifications
are noted within the bilateral internal carotid arteries.

TECHNIQUE:
Single supine view of the pelvis.

FINDINGS:
There is a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern with a moderate amount of stool
noted in the ascending colon. There is no free air demonstrated, although
diaphragms not fully evaluated. A penile implant is in place.  Degenerative
changes of the lower lumbar spine are noted. There also degenerative changes
at both femoral acetabular joints with prominent acetabular spurring.

EXAMINATION:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Multi-detector CT axial images were acquired through the abdomen
and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration using a split bolus
technique. coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to
PACS for review. Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:
DLP: 931 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis).
IV Contrast: 130 mL Omnipaque.

FINDINGS:
The exam is limited by motion artifact, particularly along the upper abdomen.

LOWER CHEST:
Dependent changes are noted in the visualized left lower lung.

HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. There
is no evidence of focal lesions. There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation. The gallbladder is distended with prominent
gallstones demonstrated within the lumen. No obstructing radio-opaque
gallstones are visualized. There is adjacent fat-stranding anterior to the
gallbladder (Series 5, Image 17; Series 7b, Image 27). There is no gallbladder
wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. No air is demonstrated within the
gallbladder lumen. There is no pneumobilia or ascites.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions, pancreatic ductal dilatation, or peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen is normal in size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrograms.
There is no evidence of stones, concerning focal renal lesions,
hydronephrosis, or perinephric abnormality. The ureters are unremarkable.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness, and enhancement throughout.  There is mild pancolonic
diverticulosis. The rectum is within normal limits. The appendix contains air
and is normal in caliber without evidence of fat stranding. There is no bowel
obstruction, pneumatosis, intra-abdominal free air, or loculated fluid
collection.

RETROPERITONEUM:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. Moderate atherosclerotic
calcified lesions are demonstrated throughout the abdominal aorta,
bifurcation, and iliac branches.

PELVIS:
The bladder is moderately distended with a anterior, right-sided
wide-mouthed, small out-pouching most consistent with a diverticulum (Series
7b, Image 39). The prostate is enlarged with a calculated prostate volume of
approximately 37 mL. Non-specific coarse calcifications are noted in the
prostate. The seminal vesicles are unremarkable. The patient has a penile
prosthesis. There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. There is no free
fluid in the pelvis.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
There is no suspicious lytic or sclerotic bony lesion
or degenerative change. A small, sclerotic bone island is noted in the left
femoral head. The abdominal pelvic walls are within normal limits.

CHEST (PA AND LAT):

TECHNIQUE:
Chest PA and lateral

FINDINGS:
Heart size is top normal. Mediastinal and hilar contours are unremarkable. The
pulmonary vasculature is normal. Streaky opacity in the left lung base may
reflect atelectasis. Subsegmental atelectasis is also noted in the right lung
base. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen. No
acute osseous abnormalities identified. Multiple clips are seen within the
right axilla compatible prior lymph node dissection.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained of the abdomen and pelvis after the
administration of intravenous contrast.  Axial images were interpreted in
conjunction with sagittal and coronal reformats.

DLP:
___ MGy-cm

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
There is mild dependent atelectasis at the right base.. The visualized
portion of the heart and pericardium are normal. There is no pericardial
effusion.

ABDOMEN:
There is stranding and fluid seen surrounding the head, body, and tail of the
pancreas, which appear to enhance normally, consistent with pancreatitis. The
pancreatic duct is prominent, although not enlarged. Multiple prominent
although nonenlarged retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are present.

The liver is normal without focal or diffuse abnormality.  The gallbladder,
intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts, and spleen are normal.  There is an
incompletely characterized 1 cm nodule of the left adrenal gland. The right
adrenal gland is somewhat thickened and lobulated but without discrete nodule.
The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete contrast promptly. The ureters
are normal in course and caliber.

The stomach is normal. The small and large bowel enhance homogeneously and
have a normal course and caliber.  There is diverticulosis without
diverticulitis.  The appendix is well visualized and normal appearing..

No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy. The portal and
intra-abdominal systemic vasculature are normal. No abdominal wall hernia,
pneumoperitoneum, or free abdominal fluid.  Abdominal aorta is normal in
caliber with scattered atherosclerotic calcifications. Other vasculature
specifically surrounding the pancreas appears patent.

PELVIS:
The bladder and terminal ureters are normal.  There is a fibroid uterus.

No pelvic side-wall or inguinal lymphadenopathy. No free pelvic fluid or
inguinal hernia.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is a chronic appearing compression deformities of
L1.  However there is a increased sclerosis within the L1 and potentially S1
vertebrae. Other degenerative changes including Schmorl's nodes seen within
the lumbar spine.

NOTIFICATION:
Additions to WET READ were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr.
___ at 615 on ___.

TECHNIQUE:
Supine and upright views of the abdomen.

FINDINGS:
There is no pneumatosis or pneumoperitoneum. The bowel gas pattern is
nonspecific but nonobstructive with moderate fecal loading in the ascending,
transverse, sigmoid colon and rectum. There are no abnormal soft tissue
calcifications. The lung bases are clear. The visualized osseous structures
are unremarkable.

EXAMINATION:
MR ___:

TECHNIQUE:
T1 and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen and pelvis
were acquired within a 1.5 T magnet, including 3D dynamic sequences performed
prior to, during, and following the administration of 0.1 mmol/kg of Gadavist
intravenous contrast (9 cc). Oral contrast consisted of 900 mL of VoLumen. 1.0
mg of Glucagon was administered IM to reduce bowel peristalsis.

FINDINGS:


MR ENTEROGRAPHY:
The MRI appearance of the small bowel is within normal limits. Specifically,
normal distensibility is seen throughout the small bowel loops without
evidence of stricture. No segmental wall thickening, edema or hyperemia.  No
mucosal thickening seen. There is no mesenteric hyperemia or fibrofatty
proliferation.

The study is not intended to evaluate the colon given lack of bowel prep.
There is a relatively large volume of fecal material throughout their the
right hemicolon. No evidence of colitis is seen. The appendix is well
visualized, normal in appearance (14:62).

MRI OF THE ABDOMEN WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:
There is a abnormal appearance of the gallbladder. There is cholelithiasis
with small stones dependently. The gallbladder is distended with a
circumferentially thickened and edematous wall. The diameter of the wall
measures up to 1 cm. There is initial mucosal enhancement, somewhat
discontinuous in appearance at times (1302:41) without dramatic
hyperenhancement. On the more delayed sequences, there is progressive
heterogeneous enhancement of the wall, particularly at the level of the fundus
(16:107). There is a small amount of free fluid surrounding the gallbladder
and extending towards the inferior tip of the liver (10:25), without fluid
seen elsewhere within the abdominal cavity. There is also a small amount of
hyperemia of the adjacent liver parenchyma (1300 01:29).

The cystic duct is unable to be visualized throughout its coarse but does not
appear dilated. There is prominence of the cystic artery.

The remainder of the liver is normal in appearance with normal parenchymal
signal and enhancement. The spleen with accessory splenic tissue, pancreas,
adrenal glands and kidneys are unremarkable.

MRI OF THE PELVIS WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:
The urinary bladder, visualized portion of the prostate and seminal vesicles
are unremarkable. There is no free pelvic fluid or pelvic lymphadenopathy.
Osseous structures are unremarkable.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Single phase contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired through the
abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 0.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 2.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 1.2
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.7 s, 53.1 cm; CTDIvol = 21.3 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,131.7 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,133 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
There is a punctate granuloma in the left lower lobe. There is
bilateral atelectasis.  There is no pericardial effusion.  There are moderate
coronary artery calcifications.  Moderate cardiomegaly

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
Scattered subcentimeter hypodensities are incompletely characterized, but
likely represent hepatic cysts or biliary hamartomas.  There is mild
periportal edema.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic
biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is distended and contains sludge.  There
is pericholecystic fat stranding, particularly surrounding the neck.  A 1.3 cm
hyperdensity near the gallbladder neck may represent an impacted gallstone
(2:28, 601:31).

PANCREAS:
The pancreas is atrophic.  There is no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.  Incidentally noted is a 7 mm accessory spleen.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
Subcentimeter hypodensities bilaterally are too small to characterize, but
statistically likely represent simple cysts.  There is no evidence of solid
renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout. Diverticulosis of
the sigmoid colon is noted, without evidence of wall thickening or fat
stranding.  There is a left inguinal hernia containing loops of nonobstructed
sigmoid colon the appendix is normal.

PELVIS:
Although the bladder is partially decompressed, there appears to be
mild haziness of the bladder wall, which could represent cystitis.  There is
no free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The prostate and seminal vesicles are grossly
unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is focal ectasia of the abdominal aorta measuring up to 3.0 cm
just proximal to the iliac bifurcation, previously 2.7 cm in ___.  Extensive
atherosclerotic disease is noted.

BONES:
Partially visualized is a left total hip arthroplasty.  There are no
suspicious osseous lesions.  There are moderate multilevel degenerative
changes in the visualized thoracolumbar spine.

SOFT TISSUES:
Aside from the previously mentioned left inguinal hernia
containing nonobstructed loops of large bowel, the abdominal and pelvic wall
is within normal limits.

TECHNIQUE:
Contrast-enhanced axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were
obtained with multiplanar reformatted images.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
Aside from hypoventilatory changes at the lung
bases, the lungs are clear without pericardial or pleural effusion.

There is marked distention of the gallbladder with pericholecystic fluid and
inflammatory fat stranding.  No radiodense gallstones are seen and no focal
fluid collections are observed. Hyperemia of the adjacent liver parenchyma is
noted. The liver, spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands appear unremarkable.
The kidneys enhance symmetrically and left hydronephrosis due to the known
ureteropelvic junction obstruction has improved compared ___.
Intra-abdominal loops of large and small bowel are of normal caliber. Patient
is status post right colonic resction and ileocolonic anastamosis. There is no
free intra- abdominal air. Atherosclerotic calcification of the abdominal
aorta is noted, though it remains of normal caliber.  Although this exam is
not tailored to evaluate arterial structures, unchanged occlusions of the
origin of the celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery are reidentified,
with retrograde filling via a widely patent re- implanted inferior mesenteric
artery.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
The rectum, sigmoid colon, uterus, adnexa, and
bladder are unremarkable.  No free fluid or pathologically enlarged pelvic
lymph nodes are seen.

Bone windows reveal no worrisome lytic or sclerotic lesions.

FINDINGS:
The cardiomediastinal silhouette is unchanged.  The pulmonary
vascularity appears normal.  The lungs remain clear without pleural effusion
or pneumothorax.  There is no evidence for pneumoperitoneum.  Dextroconvex
thoracic scoliosis is noted.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
CT SCAN OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS PERFORMED ON ___:
Comparison is made with a prior torso CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT was used to obtain contiguous axial images
through the abdomen following the administration of Visipaque IV contrast and
no oral contrast.  Axial, coronal, sagittal reformations were provided.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
The imaged lung bases are clear with note made of emphysema. 
There is no pleural effusion.  The imaged portion of the heart is
unremarkable.  There is a small hiatal hernia.

ABDOMEN:
The liver enhances normally and is without focal lesion.  There is
mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation.  A calcified gallstone is noted
impacted in the gallbladder neck with marked gallbladder wall edema.  There
are additional gallstones seen within the gallbladder lumen.  Given the
position of the large gallstone impacted in the gallbladder neck with
associated biliary ductal dilation and gallbladder wall edema, the findings
raise concern for ____ as well as probable Mirizzi syndrome. 
There is free fluid tracking inferior to the liver and gallbladder.  The
gallbladder mucosa appears grossly intact though there is subtle ill
definition of the gallbladder wall noted anteriorly on series 301B image 29
and the possibility of early perforation cannot be entirely excluded.  The
common bile duct is normal in caliber.  The pancreas appears normal.  The
spleen, adrenal glands appear normal.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically,
though excretion of contrast is seen which may be related to patient's
borderline renal function.  Recommendation for hydration post-CT was made with
Dr. ___.  Extensive vascular calcification is noted.

The stomach is decompressed.  The duodenum appears grossly unremarkable.

PELVIS:
Loops of small bowel demonstrate no evidence of ileus or obstruction.
Free fluid along the right paracolic gutter into the pelvis is noted.  The
large bowel appears grossly unremarkable.  The appendix is not clearly
visualized though there is no secondary sign of appendicitis.  The uterus and
adnexal structures appear grossly unremarkable.  The urinary bladder is
decompressed.  No pelvic side wall, mesenteric, or inguinal lymphadenopathy is
seen.

BONES:
Degenerative changes and osteopenia noted.  No worrisome lytic or
blastic osseous lesion.  Grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 is stable from

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAMINATION:
CT abdomen/pelvis with oral and intravenous contrast

TECHNIQUE:
Helical images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
following administration of oral and IV contrast material.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Total DLP = 307.19.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
Trace left pleural effusion with mild adjacent left basilar
atelectasis.

HEPATOBILIARY:
There has been interval removal of a common bile duct stent. 
There is significant pneumobilia in the common bile duct extending into the
left intrahepatic bile duct and a trace amount extending into the right
intrahepatic bile duct.  There is also gas within the cystic duct and nearly
completely filling the gallbladder.  Additionally, there is very high density
material and gas apparently within the subcapsular aspect of segment V/VIII
spanning in total approximately 4.0 x 1.3 cm (02:17).  The hepatic parenchyma
demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas is somewhat atrophic with numerous scattered
calcifications which are likely the sequela of chronic pancreatitis.  There is
no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesion or laceration.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
There is a percutaneous gastrostomy tube.  The stomach is
otherwise unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Multiple surgical clips are seen
adjacent to the second portion of the duodenum Diverticulosis of the sigmoid
colon is noted, without evidence of wall thickening and fat stranding.  The
appendix is not visualized.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm or retroperitoneal hematoma. 
Extensive atherosclerotic disease is noted.  There are stents at the origins
of the celiac and superior mesenteric arteries.  While this examination was
not tailored for evaluation of the arteries, atherosclerotic disease may cause
significant stenosis of the celiac axis, common hepatic artery, splenic
artery, as proximal superior mesenteric artery, bilateral renal arteries,
right external and internal iliac arteries, and right superficial femoral
artery.  There was the known thrombus in the celiac stent on the prior study.

BONES:
There is no acute fracture.  Anterior height loss of the T12 vertebral
body is unchanged compared ___ suggesting prior compression
fracture.  Irregularity of the posterolateral right ninth through eleventh
ribs and posterolateral left ninth and tenth ribs suggests prior fractures. 
No focal suspicious osseous abnormality.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

consistent with a proteinaceous or hemorrhagic cyst.

thickening and mild hyper enhancement of the wall of the cecum and ascending
colon.

lymphadenopathy.

superior mesenteric arteries.  There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the
visualized abdominal aorta.  The hepatic portal, superior mesenteric, and
splenic veins are patent.

low signal intensity bone may reflect iron deposition.

completely filling the gallbladder.  Additionally, there is very high density
material and gas apparently within the subcapsular aspect of segment V/VIII
spanning in total approximately 4.0 x 1.3 cm (02:17).  The hepatic parenchyma
demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.

The pancreas is somewhat atrophic with numerous scattered
calcifications which are likely the sequela of chronic pancreatitis.  There is
no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesion or laceration.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
There is a percutaneous gastrostomy tube.  The stomach is
otherwise unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Multiple surgical clips are seen
adjacent to the second portion of the duodenum Diverticulosis of the sigmoid
colon is noted, without evidence of wall thickening and fat stranding.  The
appendix is not visualized.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

of the celiac and superior mesenteric arteries.  While this examination was
not tailored for evaluation of the arteries, atherosclerotic disease may cause
significant stenosis of the celiac axis, common hepatic artery, splenic
artery, as proximal superior mesenteric artery, bilateral renal arteries,
right external and internal iliac arteries, and right superficial femoral
artery.  There was the known thrombus in the celiac stent on the prior study.

body is unchanged compared ___ suggesting prior compression
fracture.  Irregularity of the posterolateral right ninth through eleventh

EXAMINATION:
CT abdomen/pelvis with oral and intravenous contrast

TECHNIQUE:
Helical images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
following administration of oral and IV contrast material.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Total DLP = 307.19.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
Trace left pleural effusion with mild adjacent left basilar
atelectasis.

HEPATOBILIARY:
There has been interval removal of a common bile duct stent. 
There is significant pneumobilia in the common bile duct extending into the
left intrahepatic bile duct and a trace amount extending into the right
intrahepatic bile duct.  There is also gas within the cystic duct and nearly
completely filling the gallbladder.  Additionally, there is very high density
material and gas apparently within the subcapsular aspect of segment V/VIII
spanning in total approximately 4.0 x 1.3 cm (02:17).  The hepatic parenchyma
demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas is somewhat atrophic with numerous scattered
calcifications which are likely the sequela of chronic pancreatitis.  There is
no peripancreatic stranding.

SPLEEN:
The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesion or laceration.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
There is a percutaneous gastrostomy tube.  The stomach is
otherwise unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Multiple surgical clips are seen
adjacent to the second portion of the duodenum Diverticulosis of the sigmoid
colon is noted, without evidence of wall thickening and fat stranding.  The
appendix is not visualized.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm or retroperitoneal hematoma. 
Extensive atherosclerotic disease is noted.  There are stents at the origins
of the celiac and superior mesenteric arteries.  While this examination was
not tailored for evaluation of the arteries, atherosclerotic disease may cause
significant stenosis of the celiac axis, common hepatic artery, splenic
artery, as proximal superior mesenteric artery, bilateral renal arteries,
right external and internal iliac arteries, and right superficial femoral
artery.  There was the known thrombus in the celiac stent on the prior study.

BONES:
There is no acute fracture.  Anterior height loss of the T12 vertebral
body is unchanged compared ___ suggesting prior compression
fracture.  Irregularity of the posterolateral right ninth through eleventh
ribs and posterolateral left ninth and tenth ribs suggests prior fractures. 
No focal suspicious osseous abnormality.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

EXAMINATION:
MRCP:

TECHNIQUE:
T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 4.5 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

FINDINGS:
Lower Thorax: There are small right and trace left pleural effusions with
minimal adjacent atelectasis.

Liver: There is an approximately 1.5 x 1.3 cm T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense,
nonenhancing fluid collection the subcapsular aspect of segment VIII (7:9). 
There are additional, smaller T2 hyperintense foci in the subcapsular aspect
of segment VIII more laterally measuring 1.1 x 0.6 cm and 1.1 x 0.2 cm (07:10,
1502:92).  There is out of phase compared to in phase loss of signal
suggesting hemosiderin deposition.  The liver otherwise demonstrates
homogeneous signal intensity throughout with no focal lesions identified.

Biliary: There is pneumobilia within the common bile duct, cystic duct,
gallbladder, and left intrahepatic bile ducts.  There is no intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  There is an aberrant insertion of the
posterior right intrahepatic bile duct on the left intrahepatic bile duct. 
There is no peribiliary enhancement.

Pancreas: The pancreas is atrophic with no focal lesions identified.  The main
pancreatic duct is top normal in diameter at 3 mm with a somewhat lobulated
contour in keeping with known chronic pancreatitis.

Spleen: The spleen is homogeneous in signal attenuation and enhancement
throughout with out of phase compared to in phase signal loss suggesting
hemosiderin deposition.  Small enhancing focus measuring 8 mm at the upper
pole of the spleen (series 1501, image 92) may reflect a small hemangioma.

Adrenal Glands: The right and left adrenal glands are normal and symmetric in
size and shape.

Kidneys: The kidneys are symmetric and normal in size, signal intensity, and
enhancement.  There is a 4 x 6 mm T1 hyperintense, T2 hypointense,
nonenhancing lesion arising from the superior aspect of the right kidney
consistent with a proteinaceous or hemorrhagic cyst.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  A percutaneous gastrostomy tube is present.  The
stomach is otherwise grossly unremarkable.  Visualized loops of small bowel
are normal in caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement.  There is abnormal
thickening and mild hyper enhancement of the wall of the cecum and ascending
colon.

Lymph Nodes: There is no visualized retroperitoneal or mesenteric
lymphadenopathy.

Vasculature: There are vascular stents at the origins of the celiac and
superior mesenteric arteries.  There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the
visualized abdominal aorta.  The hepatic portal, superior mesenteric, and
splenic veins are patent.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: No suspicious osseous lesion.  Generally
low signal intensity bone may reflect iron deposition.

NOTIFICATION:
The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 7:14 ___, less than 30
minutes after discovery of the findings.

PA and lateral radiographs of the chest

The lungs are mildly hyperinflated with diffuse prominence of interstitial
markings and lung vasculature.  There are bilateral small pleural effusions.

arthropathy.

Bilateral pleural effusions, greater on the right with overlying atelectasis.

within normal limits.  Unchanged prominent interstitial markings bilaterally.

TECHNIQUE:
Volumetric CT imaging was performed through the abdomen and pelvis
after the administration of 130 mL Omnipaque nonionic intravenous contrast. 
Post processing performed in the coronal and sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:
The findings in the chest are reported separately.

Abdomen:  The lung bases are clear.  The liver, spleen, and pancreas are
normal.  The right adrenal is normal. This thickening of the left adrenal
without discrete nodule.  The gallbladder appears distended with a single
gallstone noted within the lumen.  The CBD appears dilated measuring up to 1.2
cm.  The cental hepatic ducts are also mildly dilated, but there is no
significant intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  There is no surrounding
inflammatory change or filling defect within the CBD on CT to suggest
____ or choledocholithiasis.  The left kidney is normal in
appearance.  The right kidney demonstrates a sub 5 mm hypodensity in the
interpolar region which is too small to accurately characterize.  There is no
hydronephrosis.  The retroperitoneum demonstrates multiple minimally enlarged
lymph nodes, specicifcally in the paraaortic and bilateral external iliac
chains.  The largest node seen is in the right external iliac chain measuring
1.5cm (2, 104).  The visualized bowel loops and mesentery are normal.  There
are atherosclerotic changes of the abdominal aorta.  The mesenteric vessels
appear patent.  The osseous structures are intact.  Again noted is the sharply
marginated endplate sclerosis involving the right right aspect of the L2-3
vertebral bodies with asymmetric disc space height loss of on the right as
well.  Appearance is similar to recent CT guided biopsy.  

Pelvis:  The visualized pelvic organs are normal.  There is no pelvic mass or
free fluid.  A well circumscribed lucent lesion is noted in the left ilium
likely representing a benign fibroosseous lesion. No acute osseous abnormality
seen.

COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OF THE THORAX:


TECHNIQUE:
Volumetric CT acquisitions over the entire thorax in inspiration,
administration of intravenous contrast material, multiplanar reconstructions.

FINDINGS:
No incidental thyroid findings.  There is a generalized increase of
slightly enlarged lymph nodes, as typically seen in HIV infection. However, no
obvious lymphadenopathy or necrotic lymph nodes are visible.  Normal
appearance of the ascending and descending aorta as well as of the aortic
arch.  Normal diameter of the pulmonary artery.  Minimal coronary artery
calcifications, minimal valvular calcifications.  Normal appearance of the
heart.  No pericardial effusion.  Minimal hiatal hernia.  Mild splenomegaly. 
For a more detailed description of the abdominal findings, please refer to the
report of the CT examination of the abdomen performed on the same date.

Moderate degenerative vertebral disease, but no evidence of osteolytic lesions
or vertebral compression fractures.  Old healed right-sided rib fractures.

The lung volumes are normal.  At the bases of the right upper lobe, there is a
very subtle and focal area with minimal ___ opacities of
non-characteristic appearance and likely caused by a previous infection. 
Generalized minimal airway wall thickening, suggesting mild chronic airways
disease.  No mucus plugging or focal airway abnormalities.  Non-characteristic
1-2 mm subpleural granulomas, for example on series 4, image 161 (that
requires no CT followup).

The pleural surfaces are even, there is no pleural effusion.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiphase, multi sequence brain MRI is obtained pre- and post
intravenous administration of 7 cc of Gadavist contrast.  The following
sequences are utilized:  Sagittal T1, axial T1 pre, axial FLAIR, axial T2,
axial susceptibility, axial DTI, axial T1 post, sagittal MPRAGE with
reformats.

FINDINGS:
There are stable scattered T2/FLAIR hyperintense foci within the white matter.
There is no infarct, mass effect or hydrocephalus.  The ventricles and
extra-axial spaces were normal in size.  There.

There is fluid within the right ethmoid and frontal ethmoidal sinus.

On the post-contrast images there is no abnormal enhancement.

The intracranial flow voids are unremarkable.

Small bilateral pleural effusions are seen.  Minimal right lower lobe
atelectasis is present.  No pulmonary nodules or masses are seen.

ABDOMEN:
Within the liver in segment VII, there is a poorly defined low-density lesion,
that measures 10 x 17 mm in diameter.  It is somewhat less well seen on the
previous CT(non-contrast), however, it was present then.  There are no new
liver lesions.  Cholecystectomy clips are seen.  The right kidney is
malrotated, however, no focal abnormality is seen in the right kidney.  The
left kidney is normal.  The spleen, pancreas, and both adrenal glands are
normal with no focal abnormality.

Again free air is seen throughout the peritoneal cavity however there is less
free air today.  No free fluid is seen within the abdomen.  There is
aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta, which is very focal, with
maximum transverse diameter of 30 x 32 mm in diameter.  There is calcification
of the abdominal aorta.No fat stranding is seen in the region of the duodenum
to suggest a perforated duodenal ulcer.

CT PELVIS:
Again there is significant artifact from the left total hip replacement,
obscuring fine detail.  

An air-filled collection is seen to lie in the left hemipelvis, lateral to the
sigmoid colon.  This measures 25 x 50 mm in diameter, when it previously
measured 16 x 55 mm in diameter.  This is almost completely filled with air
with only a trace of fluid within the dependent portion of this collection. 
The second collection, which lies anterior to the rectum also contains mainly
air with the fluid component also. It previously measured 36 x 56 mm in
diameter, and now measures 55 x 75 mm in diameter.  A third pelvic collecion
lying above the sigmoid colon measures73 x 21 mm in diamter and is nes since
the previous CT.
