visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Axial CT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
without intravenous contrast.  Note that contrast was withheld secondary to
acute renal failure.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images are also
reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT CONTRAST:
Imaged portion of the heart is notable for
cardiomegaly, partially imaged pacing devices, aortic valvular and annular
calcification as well as carotid arterial calcification.  There is a small
right pleural effusion and bibasilar subsegmental atelectasis.  Note is made
of a tiny hiatal hernia.  Dense material in the stomach, duodenum and proximal
jejunum is likely oral contrast, possibly administered in an outside hospital.
The spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, and kidneys are unremarkable, within the
confines of this non-contrast study.  The gallbladder is distended and
contains dense material, either vicarious excretion of contrast from a
previous CT or alternatively gallbladder sludge.  The liver shows no focal
mass, though is minimally nodular in contour.  Regional vascular structures
reveal extensive atherosclerotic calcification of the aorta and its primary
branches.  There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pneumoperitoneum.  Note is made of a moderate volume of ascites.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:
The urinary bladder contains a Foley catheter. 
The prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable, though evaluation of fine
details in the deep pelvis is slightly obscured by beam hardening related to a
left hip replacement.  The rectum and colon are notable for sigmoid
diverticulosis.  In the setting of ascites and the absence of contrast, the
presence or absence of ____ is difficult to evaluate.  There is no
free gas in the pelvis.  There is no pelvic sidewall or inguinal
lymphadenopathy.  Note is made of a left common femoral central venous line.

OSSEOUS FINDINGS:
As stated previously, the patient is status post left total
hip arthroplasty with imaged portions of the hardware appearing appropriately
positioned.  A small bone island is seen in the pubic bone on the right and
note is made of a remote right pubic ramus fracture.  There is no suspicious
sclerotic or lytic osseous lesion.  There is marked degenerative change
throughout the spine, with partial degenerative fusion of the fourth and fifth
lumbar vertebral bodies and loss of intervertebral disc height throughout the
entire visualized spine.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial CT images were acquired through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of 130 cc of intravenous Optiray contrast.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
Visualization of the lung bases is notable for
bibasilar atelectasis.  There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.  Limited
visualization of the heart apex is unremarkable.  There is fatty
infiltration of the liver which is otherwise unremarkable. The stomach,
proximal small bowel, spleen, pancreas, right adrenal gland,  and gallbladder
are unremarkable.  The left adrenal gland is notable for a 24 x 22mm
indeterminate nodule (2:21). The kidneys are unremarkable. The abdominal aorta
is normal in caliber.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy.  A moderate amount of intra- abdominal and retroperitoneal
free gas is noted. There is no free fluid in the abdomen.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
The rectum is unremarkable. Scattered sigmoid
diverticulae are seen with mild inflammatory fat stranding and thickening of
the sigmoid mesocolon. Adjacent to the region of sigmoid ____, there
is a large collection of extraluminal gas measuring ~55 x 31 mm (2:65),
findings consistent with perforated diverticulis. This gas is interspersed
with heterogeneous soft tissue density, concerning for extraluminal feces into
the abdomen.  The remainder of the colon is unremarkable. The appendix is well
visualized and is unremarkable. There is no pelvic side wall or inguinal
lymphadenopathy. Note is made of a partially descended right testicle (2:88).

OSSEOUS FINDINGS:
There are no suspicious sclerotic or lytic lesions.  Note
is made of bilateral pars interarticularis defects at L5 with associated
anterolisthesis of L5 over S1.  Additionally, note is made of congenitally
short pedicles resulting in a narrow central canal.  Lastly, multilevel lumbar
degenerative change results in posterior osteophytes which further narrow the
canal at L3/4.

ABDOMEN, TWO VIEWS:


FINDINGS:
There is moderate amount of stool seen in the cecum.  There is a
paucity of small bowel gas.  There is no evidence of obstruction or free air. 
The osseous structures are grossly unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
Non-contrast head CT.

FINDINGS:
There is no intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage, masses, mass effect,
or shift of normally midline structures.  The ventricles and sulci are normal
in size and configuration.  The gray and white matter differentiation is well
preserved.  There is mild bilateral ethmoid and maxillary mucosal thickening
with air-fluid levels in the maxillary and sphenoid sinuses.  Osseous
structures are unremarkable.

SINGLE VIEW OF THE ABDOMEN:
An NG tube is seen coursing below the diaphragm,
with tip in the body of the stomach.  There is a paucity of bowel gas, but no
dilated bowel loops and no evidence for obstruction are identified. The
osseous structures and surrounding soft tissues are unchanged.

TECHNIQUE:
Non-contrast head CT.

FINDINGS:
There is no intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage, infarcted major
vascular territory, mass, mass effect, or edema.  The ventricles, sulci, and
cisterns are of normal configuration and size for age and unchanged.  There is
no fracture.  A small amount of fluid is again seen in the mastoid air cells,
which are mostly clear.  Visualized paranasal sinuses demonstrate mild mucosal
thickening in right maxillary sinus.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAMINATION:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:

TECHNIQUE:
Axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
without IV contrast, as per team request given thyrotoxicosis. Oral contrast
was provided.  Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated.

TOTAL EXAM DLP:
363 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
Lung bases are clear. There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.

CT of the abdomen: Evaluation of solid abdominal viscera is limited by lack of
IV contrast.  Within this limitation, the liver is homogeneous with no focal
hepatic lesions identified. There is no intra or extrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation. The gallbladder is predominantly collapsed. The adrenal glands,
pancreas and spleen are normal. Incidental note is made of a 2.1 cm accessory
spleen. The non contrast-enhanced kidneys are normal with no evidence of
hydronephrosis or renal masses.
The stomach is collapsed. There is no evidence of small bowel obstruction. The
appendix is visualized and there is no evidence of acute appendicitis. 
Diverticula are seen along the sigmoid colon with surrounding fluid most
prominent on series 2, image 67.

The intra-abdominal aorta is of normal diameter. Vessel patency cannot be
examined in this evaluation. There are multiple mildly prominent central
mesenteric lymph nodes,  none of which meet CT size criteria for pathological
enlargement although these are striking by number. There is trace free fluid.
There is no free air.

CT of the pelvis:  Within the right pelvis there is a small amount of free
fluid and stranding near several diverticula and epiploic appendages along the
lower sigmoid.  (series 2, image 67). The uterus is normal. The urinary
bladder is normal. The rectum is contrast filled. Multiple small pelvic lymph
nodes are also noted.

Osseous structures:  No blastic or lytic lesion concerning for malignancy.

NOTIFICATION:
The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ on
the telephone on ___ at 12:24 AM.

mm somewhat rounded opacity projecting over the left mid lung may be
artifactual, although underlying pulmonary nodule is not excluded.  The right
lung is clear.  There is no focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or
pneumothorax is seen.  Cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are unremarkable.

ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND:


TECHNIQUE:
Grayscale and color Doppler images of the right upper quadrant
were obtained.  Spectral analysis of the portal vein and lesion vasculature
was performed.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates normal echogenicity.  A 7.8 x 8.2 x 8.5 cm
complex cystic lesion with multiple internal septations is noted in the liver
dome which was not present in prior exam.  The thick internal septations
demonstrate arterial flow as demonstrated by spectral analysis.

Otherwise, the remaining of the liver is unremarkable.  There is no
intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation.  The gallbladder demonstrates a 0.4 xm
polyp in its neck but no wall thickening or cholelithiasis. The common bile
duct is not dilated, measuring 6 mm. The portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. The head and body of the pancreas are unremarkable. The
pancreatic tail is not visualized due to bowel gas artifact. The spleen is
normal in size, 7.6 cm.  Limited views of the aorta and inferior vena cava are
unremarkable.  There is no ascites.  

The right kidney measures 10.8 cm and the left kidney measures 10.9 cm.  The
right kidney is within normal limits, without evidence of hydronephrosis,
nephrolithiasis, or focal lesion.  There is normal corticomedullary
differentiation.  In the upper pole of the left kidney, there is 3.8 x 3.3 x
3.2 cm cystic lesion with one thin internal septation slightly  increased in
size compared with ___ when it measured 2.9 cm.  In the lower pole of the
left kidney, there are two simple cysts of which the largest measures 2.5 x
2.0 x 1.8 cm.  These two cysts are not significantly changed in size compared
with prior exam.  There is no left-sided hydronephrosis or nephrolithiasis.

TECHNIQUE:
Sagittal T1, T2, STIR and axial T2 weighted images were acquired
through the  cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine without intravenous contrast
due to acute renal failure.

FINDINGS:

alignment.  There is mild height loss of the C5 and C6 vertebral bodies, which
is likely chronic given the absence of stir hyperintensity.  The spinal cord
is normal in signal characteristics.  Visualized posterior fossa structures
are normal.  There is disc desiccation and loss of intervertebral disc height
throughout the cervical spine.  No fluid collection is identified.  

At C2-C3, there is a broad-based disc protrusion without significant cananl or
foraminal narrowing.

At C3-C4, there is a central disc protrusion all which mildly narrows the
spinal canal.  Facet and uncovertebral joint degenerative changes results in
bilateral moderate neural foraminal narrowing.  

At C4-C5, there is a left paracentral disc protrusion which contacts and
indents the spinal cord without is cord signal abnormality.  There is mild to
moderate right neural foraminal narrowing and mild left neural foraminal
narrowing. 

At C5-C6, there is a large broad-based disc protrusion with a superimposed
left paracentral protrusion with an annular tear which results in deformity of
the spinal cord with effacement of the CSF spaces.  There is severe spinal
canal narrowing.  Facet and uncovertebral joint osteophytes result in
bilateral severe neural foraminal narrowing. 

At C6-C7, there is a broad-based disk protrusion eccentric to the left which
results in spinal cord flattening and remodeling without signal abnormality. 
There is moderate spinal canal narrowing and no significant neural foraminal
narrowing.  

The C7-T1 level is unremarkable.  

The paravertebral soft tissues are normal.  

Thoracic spine:  There is convex left scoliotic curvature.  The vertebral
bodies are normal in height, signal intensity, and alignment.  There is disc
desiccation and loss of disc height, with paracentral disc protrusions at
T2-T3, T3-T4, and T5-T6 largest at T3-T4.  There is no fluid collection.  The
spinal cord is normal in signal intensity and caliber.  There is no
significant spinal canal or neural foraminal stenosis.  

Lumbar spine: the vertebral bodies are normal in height and alignment. There
are degenerative endplate marrow signal changes at L5-S1, ___ type 2.  There
is disc desiccation and loss of intervertebral disc height. The distal spinal
cord and conus medullaris is normal in appearance, with the conus terminating
at approximately the L2 level. 

There is a partially evaluated disc bulge at L2-L3 which results in mild
spinal canal narrowing and mild right neural foraminal narrowing. 

At L3-L4, there is a diffuse disc bulge, ligamentum flavum thickening, facet
degenerative changes resulting in mild spinal canal narrowing, mild to
moderate right neural foraminal narrowing, and mild left neural foraminal
narrowing. 

At L4-L5, there is a diffuse disc bulge as well as a 2.2 x 1.1 cm superiorly
migrated structure which appears contiguous with the adjacent disc and is
similar in signal characteristics to the disc. This therefore likely
represents an extruded disc fragment. It is more prominent than on prior. In
combination with ligamentum flavum thickening and facet degenerative changes,
these findings result in severe spinal canal narrowing with near complete
obliteration of the thecal sac, moderate right neural foraminal narrowing, and
moderate left neural foraminal narrowing.  

At L5-S1, there is a diffuse disc bulge with central protrusion, ligamentum
flavum thickening, and facet degenerative change resulting in mild spinal
canal narrowing, moderate right neural foraminal narrowing, and severe left
neural foraminal narrowing.  This is similar to prior exam. 

The paravertebral soft tissues are unremarkable. Multiple T2 hyperintense
structures are noted in the left kidney most likely representing cysts.

TECHNIQUE:
PA and lateral radiographs of the chest.

FINDINGS:
There appears to be interval improvement of the previously seen
vascular congestion.  There is no evidence of frank interstitial edema.  No
focal consolidations are identified.  There is no pneumothorax.  There is a
small left-sided pleural effusion.  No new focal consolidations are
identified.  The heart size is unremarkable.  The hilar and mediastinal
contours are otherwise unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplasic CT of the abdomen and pelvis including noncontrast,
arterial and venous plase imaging. Multiplanar reformats provided.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
There has been interval enlargement of large paraesophageal
hiatal hernia, with retained air and fluid contents.  Moderate emphysema is
seen at the lung bases.  There are peripheral fibrotic changes, suggestive of
interstitial lung disease.  Some bibasilar atelectasis is also present.  There
are no pleural or pericardial effusions.  Calcifications are present in the
aortic valve and left anterior descending coronary artery.

ABDOMEN:
A collection of free air is noted anterior to the liver, and
outlining bowel loops in the right upper quadrant.  At the root of the
mesentery, a few locules of gas are also present, along with a small amount of
simple fluid collection and minimal soft tissue stranding.  Trace free fluid
is also noted tracking into the perisplenic region, bilateral paracolic
gutters, and pelvis.

The stomach and small bowel are unremarkable.  Colonic diverticulosis is noted
without definite evidence of diverticilis. There is no bowel dilation to
suggest obstruction.  No abnormal wall thickening, enhancement, pneumatosis,
or mesenteric or portal venous gas to suggest bowel ischemia.

The liver enhances homogeneously, without focal masses.  Stable intrahepatic
biliary dilatation is noted, secondary to prior cholecystectomy.  There is
moderate atrophy of the pancreas, with scattered cystic-appearing lesions that
are consistent with known IPMN.  The spleen is unremarkable.  

The adrenals are normal.  The kidneys are slightly atrophic with cortical
thinning and lobulation.  However, contrast enhancement and excretion are
preserved.  A 1.5-cm simple cyst is present in the left renal interpole. 
Other scattered renal hypodensities are too small to characterize.

PELVIS:
Multiple calcified fibroids are present in the uterus.  The bladder
is normal.  Moderate atheromatous disease is noted in the abdominal aorta and
iliac arteries, with dense calcifications and irregular soft plaques.  There
is mild-to-moderate stenosis of branch artery origins, but distal perfusion is
preserved.  Retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are not pathologically
enlarged.

There is diffuse osseous demineralization and degenerative changes of the
thoracolumbar spine, most severe at L1-L2.  Grade 1 retrolisthesis is present
at L4-5.  Posterior fusion hardware is present in the L3-L5 vertebral ___,
without evidence of hardware loosening, fragmentation, or other complications.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___.:
___.

FINDINGS:
PA and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  The patient is
significantly rotated to her left which limits the evaluation.  There is
bibasilar opacity which could represent atelectasis, though at the left lung
base, the possibility of pneumonia is not excluded.  A retrocardiac gas-filled
structure is again noted compatible with a hiatal hernia.  Along the right
hemidiaphragm, a linear density with underlying lucency could reflect
platelike atelectasis though the possibility of pneumoperitoneum is
considered.

SUPINE AND ERECT ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPH:
Nonspecific non-obstructive bowel gas
pattern is noted.  Surgical clips are seen extending along the left abdomen. 
Fixation hardware is seen projecting from L3 to L5.  No free air is noted.

MRCP (MR ___:

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were acquired through the
abdomen on a 1.5 Tesla magnet, including dynamic images obtained prior to,
during, and following the uneventful intravenous administration of (12 mL) of
Gadavist.  In addition, the patient received Gadavist mixed with water orally.

FINDINGS:
The gallbladder is mildly distended and contains multiple filling defects
consistent with gallstones. There is a mild degree of gallbladder wall edema.
Following the administration of gadolinium, mild hyper enhancement within the
hepatic parenchyma about the gallbladder fossa is noted compatible with
inflammatory changes. There is mild diffuse dilation of the extrahepatic and
central intrahepatic bile ducts with the CBD measuring up to 9 mm.  The
pancreatic duct is prominent, measuring 4 mm in the pancreatic head.  No
stones are identified along the majority of the bile ducts, however, axial
HASTE images show a punctate low signal intensity focus, in the distal most
portion of the protruding ampulla (06:44), with a tiny associated focus of
high signal intensity on precontrast T1 weighted images (11:120). This could
either represent the tiny gallstone lodged in the protruding ampulla or
alternatively a small amount of reflux of oral contrast into the distal
portion of the ampulla after passage of the stone.  Peripancreatic
inflammatory change consisting of stranding and small amounts of fluid is
noted. The pancreas shows mild heterogeneous loss of signal intensity on
precontrast T1 weighted images, compatible with inflammatory changes, but
shows no evidence of necrosis.  There are no focal fluid collections and no
vascular complications of ____ are noted. Replaced left hepatic
artery is present. The celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, are widely
patent.

The liver shows diffuse patchy steatosis.  A tiny cyst or biliary hamartoma is
present peripherally in segment ___.  No concerning focal liver lesions
identified. Portal vein is patent.

In the interpolar region of the right kidney, a 2.5 cm cyst contains layering
debris of varying signal intensities consistent with a hemorrhagic or
proteinaceous contents, without evidence of enhancement. Additional
hemorrhagic cyst without internal enhancement measures 1.6 cm in the lower
pole of right kidney (11 302:128).  Additional scattered cysts are simple
within the right and left kidneys.  Adrenal glands appear normal.  Spleen and
accessory spleen appear within normal limits.  There is a trace left pleural
effusion and left lower lobe atelectasis.  Abdominal loops of bowel appear
within normal limits.

NOTIFICATION:
The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ on the
telephone on ___ at 8:36 AM, 5 minutes after discovery of the findings.

ABDOMEN (SUPINE AND ERECT):

Portable radiographs of the abdomen

The bowel gas pattern is nonobstructive with gas-filled loops of ascending and
transverse colon as well as mid abdominal and right lower quadrant small bowel
loops that do not meet strict criteria for dilatation. There are no air-fluid
levels or pneumatosis. There is no intraperitoneal free air.

Osseous structures are notable for moderate degenerative changes.

Two small radiodensities projecting over the lower pole of the left kidney are
likely small renal stones, each measuring less than 3 mm.

Incidental note is made of an IVC filter.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Volumetric CT acquisition of the abdomen and pelvis was performed
both before and after administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque 350 IV contrast
material.  Oral contrast was also administered.  Post processing
reconstruction was performed in the coronal and sagittal planes.

DLP 1127.8.:

FINDINGS:
The lung bases are clear.  There is a small amount of perihepatic and
peripancreatic ascites.  The liver is enlarged.  No intrahepatic mass is
visualized, although perfusion remains mildly heterogeneous.  There are mild
inflammatory changes surrounding the pancreas, new from prior CT.  The portal
vein, splenic vein, and SMA remain patent.  The pancreas enhances normally. 
No defined fluid collection is present to suggest abscess or pseudocyst.  The
spleen is enlarged, measuring 17.7 cm.  The gallbladder, adrenal glands, and
kidneys are normal.  Loops of small and large bowel are normal in caliber. 
There is a small amount of free fluid in the pelvis.  Numerous small
retroperitoneal lymph nodes are present, which are not pathologically
enlarged.  Normal appearance of the urinary bladder.  Incidentally noted L4
limbus vertebra.  No acute osseous abnormality is visualized.

ABDOMEN:


FINDINGS:
The visible part of the Dobbhoff catheter shows a normal course. 
The catheter, however, projects with its tip over the middle parts of the
stomach.  It is no longer in post-pyloric position, as seen on the chest x-ray
from ___.  No evidence of complications, no free air.

FINDINGS:
The bowel gas pattern is normal.  And gas is seen in nondistended loops of
large and small bowel.  

There is no evidence of intraperitoneal free air.  There is no ileus or
obstruction. 

The bony structures are unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis were
obtained following the uneventful administration of oral contrast and 75 cc of
Omnipaque intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
performed at 5 mm slice thickness.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:
An endotracheal tube terminates 2.4 cm above the carina (601B:40).  Motion
artifact limits the ability to assess finer detail of the lung parenchyma;
however, multifocal consolidations are seen throughout both lungs (2:18,
601B:43).  The heart is mildly enlarged (2:30).  The great vessels are patent
and normal in caliber.  Segmental and subsegmental evaluation of the pulmonary
arterial branches is not possible given the extensive motion artifacts. A
right-sided PICC and right IJ terminate at the lower SVC (2:19).

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
A nasogastric tube terminates within the stomach (2:62).  Multiple loops of
distended small and large bowel are present, with the small bowel measuring up
to 2.6 cm. There is no transition point.

The liver is enlarged and the hepatic parenchyma enhances heterogeneously
along the periphery, also seen on prior CT examinations, reflecting known
history of hepatitis.  The gallbladder, pancreas, adrenal glands, and kidneys
appear normal.  The spleen is mildly enlarged (601B:34).  A small recanalized
paraumbilical vein (2:68) and perisplenic varices denote chronic portal
hypertension.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and
no free air or free fluid.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
A small fat-containing right inguinal hernia is present (2:113).  A rectal
drain is place (2:119).  A Foley catheter terminates within the collapsed
bladder, which contains a small amount of intracystic gas (2:113).  There is
no intrapelvic lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is no acute fracture.  There are no bony lesions concerning for
malignancy or infection.  A chronic superior/anterior corner fracture at L4 is
unchanged in orientation in comparison to the ___ reference CT
examination (602B:39).

both before and after administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque 350 IV contrast

reconstruction was performed in the coronal and sagittal planes.

DLP 1127.8.:

The lung bases are clear.  There is a small amount of perihepatic and
peripancreatic ascites.  The liver is enlarged.  No intrahepatic mass is
visualized, although perfusion remains mildly heterogeneous.  There are mild
inflammatory changes surrounding the pancreas, new from prior CT.  The portal
vein, splenic vein, and SMA remain patent.  The pancreas enhances normally.

kidneys are normal.  Loops of small and large bowel are normal in caliber.

retroperitoneal lymph nodes are present, which are not pathologically
enlarged.  Normal appearance of the urinary bladder.  Incidentally noted L4
limbus vertebra.  No acute osseous abnormality is visualized.

ABDOMEN:


FINDINGS:

stomach.  It is no longer in post-pyloric position, as seen on the chest x-ray
from ___.  No evidence of complications, no free air.

FINDINGS:
The bowel gas pattern is normal.  And gas is seen in nondistended loops of
large and small bowel.  

There is no evidence of intraperitoneal free air.  There is no ileus or
obstruction. 

The bony structures are unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis were
obtained following the uneventful administration of oral contrast and 75 cc of
Omnipaque intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
performed at 5 mm slice thickness.

artifact limits the ability to assess finer detail of the lung parenchyma;
however, multifocal consolidations are seen throughout both lungs (2:18,
601B:43).  The heart is mildly enlarged (2:30).  The great vessels are patent

arterial branches is not possible given the extensive motion artifacts. A
right-sided PICC and right IJ terminate at the lower SVC (2:19).

distended small and large bowel are present, with the small bowel measuring up
to 2.6 cm. There is no transition point.

along the periphery, also seen on prior CT examinations, reflecting known
history of hepatitis.  The gallbladder, pancreas, adrenal glands, and kidneys
appear normal.  The spleen is mildly enlarged (601B:34).  A small recanalized

hypertension.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and

no intrapelvic lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

malignancy or infection.  A chronic superior/anterior corner fracture at L4 is
unchanged in orientation in comparison to the ___ reference CT
examination (602B:39).

The visualized right lobe of the liver is slightly echogenic, which likely
relates to steatosis, although other forms of liver disease including
steatohepatitis, cirrhosis and fibrosis can have similar imaging findings.  

No ___ fluid is identified.  No significant ascites is evident in any
quadrant of the abdomen.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis from the
level of the lung bases to the pubic symphysis after administration of the
intravenous contrast.  Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated and
reviewed.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The visualized lung bases appear normal.
There is no pleural effusion.  Visualized portion of the heart appears
unremarkable, with no evidence of pericardial effusion.

Multiple tiny subcentimeter hypodense lesions are noted in the liver (2:15 and
2:17), too small to characterize and are stable since the prior study.  There
is a stable dilatation of the intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts,  with a
dilated common bile duct measuring 15.6 mm (300B:26).  The patient is status
post cholecystectomy with surgical clips noted in the gallbladder bed.  The
pancreatic duct appears normal.  The adrenal glands and the spleen appear
unremarkable.  Again noted are tiny punctate calcifications in the pancreatic
parenchyma in the region of the tail and head of the pancreas, unchanged since
the prior study.  There is no evidence of ____.  Both kidneys
show multiple subcentimeter hypodensities, too small to characterize and most
probably represent renal cortical cysts.  Both kidneys show symmetric
opacification and excretion of contrast.  No hydroureteronephrosis noted.  The
stomach and small bowel appear unremarkable.  Multiple diverticulae are seen
diffusely distributed through the colon.

There is no evidence of intra-abdominal free fluid or free air.  There is no
significant retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The bladder is distended with no wall
thickening or internal filling defect.  The uterus is status post
transabdominal hysterectomy. There is stranding in the left pelvis, extending
along the anterior abdominal wall and subcutaneous soft tissues,  in the
region of the surgical access for hysterectomy.  There is a fluid collection
with ___ value of 29, seen along the left lateral pelvic wall, causing lateral
displacement of the left ureter. The collection has an enhancing wall and
measures 2.7 x 1.6 cm. There are multiple diverticula in the distal sigmoid
colon.  

The diagnostic consideration in this patient would include a postoperative
pelvic abscess with surrounding inflammatory fat stranding, related to the
recent hysterectomy.The diagnosis of sigmoid diverticulitis with pelvic
abscess is a less likely possibility due to the following reasons- the absence
of a culprit diverticulum ,  fat stranding localized more to the left lateral
pelvic wall and not centred around the sigmoid colon ,  absence of reactive
colonic wall thickening and the pelvic abscess located farther away from the
sigmoid diverticuli.

A small stable right inguinal hernia containing small bowel is again noted.
There is no pelvic free fluid.  There is no significant pelvic lymphadenopathy
detected.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES AND SOFT TISSUES:
Diffuse degenerative changes noted in
the distal thoracic and lumbar spine, with grade 1 anterolisthesis of L5 on S1
with bilateral pars interarticularis defect.  Also noted are ossific densities
in the bilateral gluteal subcutaneous soft tissue, most likely representing
injection granulomas.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT of the abdomen and pelvis was performed with IV
contrast only. Multiplanar reformations were provided.

DOSE:
DLP 846 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:
Lung Bases:  Mild basilar atelectasis is noted without pleural effusion. The
imaged heart is within normal limits of size without pericardial effusion
seen. A small hiatal hernia is noted.

Abdomen: The liver enhances normally without focal lesion. The gallbladder is
unremarkable. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilation is seen.
The spleen is unremarkable though a small amount of perisplenic free fluid is
noted. There is a metallic bullet-shaped foreign body adjacent to the left
twelfth rib, unchanged. Surgical clips are seen adjacent to the distal body of
the pancreas.  There is peripancreatic fat stranding which is concerning for
____.  No signs of pancreatic necrosis or pseudocyst formation.
Adrenal glands are normal bilaterally. The kidneys enhance symmetrically and
excrete contrast promptly. Fat containing lesion arising from the lower pole
of the left kidney is most compatible with an AML. Hypodense simple cysts in
the right kidney are noted as well as tiny hypodensities too small to
characterize. The gallbladder appears normal. The abdominal aorta is normally
opacified with normal course and caliber with widely patent major branches. No
retroperitoneal hematoma or lymphadenopathy is seen.

The stomach and duodenum appear normal.

Pelvis: Loops of small bowel demonstrate no signs of ileus or obstruction. 
Surgical clips are noted in the left mid abdomen.  No signs of appendicitis.
The colon appears unremarkable aside from the presence of scattered
diverticulosis.  The uterus is absent. No adnexal masses are seen. No free
pelvic fluid. The urinary bladder is only partially distended.  No inguinal
lymphadenopathy.

Bones: No worrisome lytic or blastic osseous lesion is seen.    Degenerative
changes are mild with Schmorl's nodes at L4 level.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:


TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
with oral and intravenous contrast.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were
also performed.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN:
Patchy opacities, dependent portions of the lower lungs are most
consistent with atelectasis.  There is no pleural effusion.

The liver, gallbladder, spleen, and adrenal glands appear within normal
limits.  There is mild fat stranding about the pancreas which demonstrated
slight fullness.  A small hypodense focus in the interpolar region of the
right kidney measuring 4 mm is too small to characterize but unchanged.  

There is new mild left-sided hydronephrosis, and the left ureter is moderately
dilated down to the pelvic inlet after which its course is difficult to
follow.  There is a small calcification near the left ureterovesical junction,
but already present before and probably a phlebolith lying near the area.  Fat
stranding is present about the left kidney and the nephrogram is slightly
delayed.  The left renal vein is mildly narrowed as it crosses beneath
superior mesenteric artery, which arises from the aorta at a highly acute
angle. 

The patient is status post colectomy.  There is a rectal stump with persistent
inflammatory mucosal enhancement, mild wall thickening, and surrounding fat
stranding.

CT PELVIS:
Intermingled with small bowel along the superior aspect of the
bladder to the right of midline is a small rim well-circumscribed focus of gas
and fluid which is suspected to represent a segment of small bowel within the
pelvis, noting collapsed but poorly delineated small bowel in the area, but it
is difficult to exclude a small fluid collection measuring up to perhaps 28 x
13 mm in axial ___ (2:64).  There are also small tubular
fluid-containing structures along each pelvic sidewall, but quite small and

EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Helical CT acquisition was performed DURING SINGLE PHASE after the
administration of nonionic IV contrast. Oral contrast was also administered.
Multiplanar reformats were obtained.

DOSE:
303 mGy*cm

FINDINGS:
Partial visualized left larger than right small pleural effusions with passive
atelectasis.

No focal liver lesions identified.  Post cholecystectomy.  Patent SMV, splenic
vein, portal venous system. Homogeneous appearance of the pancreas without
apparent focal lesion or main ductal dilation.  A small amount of ascites is
present throughout the abdomen and pelvis. Fat stranding is noted throughout
the anterior pararenal space adjacent to the pancreas, with mild generalized
retroperitoneal fat stranding.

Normal spleen and adrenals.

No hydronephrosis.  A tiny peripheral subcentimeter midpole left renal
hypodensity, probable cyst or angiomyolipoma.

Contrast within stomach. Mildly thickened distal duodenal folds. Contrast and
stool within the colon. The retrocecal appendix contains contrast and
demonstrates no more adjacent fat stranding in the remainder of the abdomen
and pelvis. Normal TI. No small bowel dilation.

Normal caliber abdominal aorta. Patent celiac trunk and SMA.

Nondistended bladder. Retroverted anteflexed uterus. No pelvic adenopathy.

Mild within evident total spine. No suspicious osseous lesions.

EXAMINATION:
CHEST (PA AND LAT):

FINDINGS:
PA and lateral views of the chest provided.

Moderate, bilateral pleural effusions are seen. Bilateral, lower lung
opacities likely represent moderate bibasilar atelectasis more likely than
pneumonia. Imaged osseous structures are intact.

Second opinion CT abdomen/pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:
Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:
Unavailable.  Study performed at outside hospital.

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
Limited evaluation of the lung bases is notable for a small left
non hemorrhagic pleural effusion

ABDOMEN:


HEPATOBILIARY:
The liver is diffusely heterogeneous in signal intensity with
multiple peripheral low-density opacities scattered throughout the liver when
compared to in and out of phase imaging from outside MR demonstrates signal
drop on out of phase imaging consistent with focal hepatic steatosis.  Along
the hepatic capsule adjacent to segment 2 is a multiloculated approximately 2
x 3 x 1.7 cm collection along the gastrohepatic ligament (02:18).  There is no
evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder
is within normal limits.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas is diffusely heterogeneous in signal intensity with
mild dilatation of the main pancreatic duct with few cystic structures within
the body and tail measuring up to 0.2 x 0.6 cm (02:27).  Peripancreatic fat
stranding is noted.  There hypoenhancement within the pancreatic head
worrisome for pancreatic necrosis (02:42).

SPLEEN:
Normal in size.  No splenomegaly.  Mild perisplenic free fluid noted. 
1.4 cm accessory spleen is noted.

ADRENALS:
The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:
The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
The stomach is unremarkable.  Loss of normal fat plane
between the pancreatic head and duodenum with fat stranding along the distal
stomach and duodenum.  Small bowel loops otherwise demonstrate normal caliber,
wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and rectum are within
normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized however no secondary signs of
acute appendicitis.  No extraluminal air.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS:
The visualized reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  No atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES:
There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES:
The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___:
Comparison is made with a prior chest radiograph from ___ as well as a CT
abdomen and pelvis from approximately 10 minutes later same day.

FINDINGS:
PA and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  Lungs are clear
bilaterally demonstrating no evidence of pneumonia or CHF.  There is mild
atelectasis at the left lung base.  Lungs are otherwise clear bilaterally.
There is hyperlucent appearance of the lungs which is compatible with
underlying emphysema seen on a prior CT chest from ___.  There is mild
prominence of the pulmonary hila which may be related to underlying pulmonary
arterial hypertension. Clinical correlation is advised. No free air is seen
below the right hemidiaphragm.  A metallic aortic stent is partially
visualized in the upper abdomen.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were obtained from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis without administration of intravenous contrast due to the patient's
elevated creatinine.  Multiplanar coronal and sagittal reformatted images were
generated.

NONCONTRAST CT ABDOMEN:
linear and nodular opacity in the lingula (2:3) is
most compatible with atelectasis.  The lung bases are otherwise clear.  There
is no pleural effusion or pericardial effusion.

There is extensive peripancreatic inflammatory stranding and fluid with
thickening of the lateral conal fascia. Findings are consistent with acute
____. There is no focal fluid collection. Evaluation for pancreatic
necrosis or splenic vein thrombosis is limited on this noncontrast CT.  The
spleen is normal in size. The liver is diffusely low in attenuation consistent
with fatty infiltration, with focal sparing along the gallbladder fossa.

The small bowel, stomach and colon are normal in caliber. An exophytic right
renal cyst measures 3 cm in diameter. There is no hydronephrosis. Mild
perinephric stranding is symmetric and nonspecific.  The adrenal glands appear
normal.

An endovascular aortic stent graft is again seen with position unchanged from
___. The infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm is decreased in size
from previous study, now measuring 3.1 x 3.6 cm (previously 3.8 x 4.4 cm).
There are no enlarged abdominal lymph nodes.

NON-CONTRAST CT PELVIS:
A small amount of fluid layers dependently in the
pelvis (2:76).  The rectum is within normal limits.  There are diverticula
predominantly of the descending and sigmoid colon, without evidence for
diverticulitis.  Pelvic loops of small bowel are normal in caliber.  The
urinary bladder has an unremarkable non-contrast CT appearance. The prostate
is enlarged, measuring 5.7 cm in diameter, with internal calcifications,
unchanged from ___.  There are bilateral fat-containing inguinal hernias.

BONES:
Bone windows demonstrate no lesions suspicious for malignancy.  There
are degenerative changes of the lumbar spine, with vacuum disc phenomenon and
loss of intervertebral disc space at L5-S1.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
The liver is diffusely echogenic and
there is coarsened echotexture which limits evaluation.  The gallbladder is
non-distended.  A small amount of pericholecystic fluid correlates with the
findings of the CT.  Sonographic ___ sign is negative.  There are no
gallstones.  There is no intra-hepatic ductal dilation.  The common duct is at
the upper limits of normal, measuring 8 mm in diameter.  The pancreas is not
well seen.  A right upper pole renal cyst measures 3.5 x 2.9 x 3.8 cm.  There
is no right hydronephrosis.  There is a small amount of ascites adjacent to
the liver and spleen.  The spleen is not enlarged.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the thoracic inlet down to the
pubic symphysis with oral contrast.

CT OF THE CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST:
The bilateral lungs show pleural effusions, left greater than right, with
associated lobar collapse.  The visualized heart is unremarkable.  No axillary
or mediastinal lymphadenopathy seen.

An ET tube is seen ending within the trachea.  A right internal jugular
catheter is seen ending in the distal superior vena cava.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH ENTERAL CONTRAST:
The liver is normal in size with surrounding ascitic fluid.

The spleen, bilateral adrenal glands, and bilateral kidneys are unremarkable
with the exception of a benign cyst arising from the mid pole region of the
right kidney.

There are significant inflammatory changes surrounding the pancreas with
significant amount of stranding and almost phlegmonous appearance of the
pancreas.  There is no fluid collection, pancreatic pseudocyst formation.
These inflammatory changes extend throughout the abdomen with fluid
collections tracking down the bilateral paracolic gutters into the pelvis.
Stranding is also seen throughout the mesentry, all consistent with the
patient's presentation of severe ____.

No abdominal lymphadenopathy is seen.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH ENTERAL CONTRAST:
A Foley catheter is seen with its balloon inflated within the bladder.  The
seminal vesicles, prostate, bladder, rectum, and sigmoid colon are
unremarkable.  Bilateral fat-filled inguinal hernias are seen.  There is
significant amount of third spacing and fluid within the subcutaneous tissues.
Incidental note is made of an aortic graft.  Also seen is a biliary stent,
seen in good position.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable with
no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions seen.  There is some mild degenerative
disease seen.

visible_prior_imaging.exam: LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN) PORT
visible_prior_imaging.report:
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
The liver is diffusely increased in
echogenicity and coarsened in echotexture, consistent with fatty infiltration;
this markedly attenuates sonographic penetration, limiting evaluation.

The gallbladder is not visualized, which can be explained by the presence of
air filling most of the lumen on a recent CT. If the appearance were the same
as on the recent CT, when the gallbladder was not distended and contained air
suggesting patency of the cystic duct, lack of visualization would be
expected.  Accordingly, it is likely there has been no significant change,
noting no distended fluid-filled gallbladder can be identified. The main
portal vein demonstrates hepatopetal flow. There is a trace amount of
perihepatic ascites, as seen on the recent CT torso.

EXAM:
Renal ultrasound obtained ___.

CORRELATION:
CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiple static grayscale images through the abdomen were obtained
and submitted for evaluation.

FINDINGS:
The right kidney measures 11.1 cm.  There is no hydronephrosis or
renal calculi are identified.  Along the upper pole is a 2.9 x 2.7 x 2.1 cm
hypoechoic structure with posterior acoustic enhancement.  On comparison with
prior CTs, this is consistent with the known renal cyst.

The left kidney measures 10.1 cm.  There is no hydronephrosis, calculi, or
masses identified.  The cortical echotexture is maintained.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial CT images were acquired through the abdomen in the absence
of intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also
reviewed.

FINDINGS:
Moderate bilateral pleural effusions are redemonstrated with
associated bibasilar atelectasis.  The included portion of the cardiac apex is
unremarkable.  An orogastric tube courses beyond the stomach into the proximal
duodenum.  The spleen, adrenal glands appear unremarkable.  A stent is present
in the distal common bile duct with consequent pneumobilia as well as gas
within the gallbladder.  Apart from pneumobilia, the liver is unremarkable.
Note is made of a moderate amount of ascites.  The kidneys redemonstrate a
right renal hypodensity, characterized a cyst on a previous ultrasound.

Extensive peripancreatic inflammation consistent with known ____ is
redemonstrated.  On this non-contrast study, tissue enhancement and thus
necrosis is not assessed.  In addition, no assessment is made regarding
patency of the adjacent venous vasculature or the presence of pseudoaneurysms.
There is no distinct pseudocyst formation and overall, the degree of
peripancreatic and mesenteric fat stranding appears minimally progressed from
the previous study.  Specifically, there is additional hypodense material just
anterior to the pancreas.  The abdominal aorta is notable for aortic stent
graft. The included osseous structures reveal no suspicious sclerotic or lytic
lesion.

patency of the adjacent venous vasculature or the presence of pseudoaneurysms.

peripancreatic and mesenteric fat stranding appears minimally progressed from

anterior to the pancreas.  The abdominal aorta is notable for aortic stent

lesion.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
This study was imported from an outside institution for re-review.
A second opinion interpretation was requested as only a brief verbal report of
the study was known at the time.  MDCT-acquired axial images of the abdomen
and pelvis were obtained with IV and oral contrast at 5-mm slice thickness. 
Additional coronal and sagittal reconstructions were performed at 3-mm slice
thickness.

FINDINGS:
Included views of the lungs demonstrate mild dependent atelectasis
bilaterally.  There is no pericardial or pleural effusion.  The heart size is
top normal.

A large multicystic mass is seen at the head of the pancreas (2:32), measuring
up to 50 x 47 mm axially.  Coarse internal calcifications are seen (2:34). 
There are multiple irregular septations with varying thickness.  This lesion
abuts the second portion of the duodenum, where there is asymmetric wall
thickening (2:31).  Neighboring fat stranding is present.  The distal pancreas
appears normal.  The pancreatic duct is not dilated, measuring 3 mm.  The
portal vein, SMV, and splenic veins are patent and appear separate from the
lesion.  The SMA is preserved. A prominent retrocrural node (2:29) does not
meet CT criteria for lymphadenopathy.

The CBD is normal in caliber.  The gallbladder is unremarkable.  A 15 mm right
hepatic cyst is present (2:11).  Other subcentimeter hypodense lesions within
the liver (2: 11,25,29) are too small for further characterization.  The
spleen, adrenal glands, stomach, and kidneys are normal.  Mild atherosclerotic
calcification of the abdominal aorta is present.  There is no mesenteric
lymphadenopathy, and no free air or free fluid. 

The rectum, sigmoid colon, intrapelvic loops of small and large bowel,
bladder, uterus, and adnexa appear normal. There is no intrapelvic
lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is no acute fracture or dislocation.  No concerning
blastic or lytic lesions are seen.  Anterior osteophytosis at L2/3 is seen.

baseline.patient_history: ___ yo morbidly obese male with history of DM II, CAD s/p CABG, chronic bilateral lymphedema, and obesity hypoventilation syndrome presented with intermittent LUQ abdominal pain. He initially presented to the OSH with fever to 102.9, and a sharp, intense, stabbing pain awoke him from sleep. It was initially LUQ pain but radiated to the RUQ. He took a double dose of his pain medication and the pain went away. He tried to avoid pain medication later in the day, but the pain came back. He also notes red extremities, but denies cough, SOB, CP, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, or diarrhea. He presented to the OSH for this acute worsening of his abdominal pain. He was found to have a transaminitis with an elevated lipase. His urine was clear after antibiotics. Zosyn was started for empiric coverage of his cellulitic process and for intraabdominal coverage. He was given Dilaudid with subsequent somnolence. ABG at that time revealed 7.28/81/52/38. All narcotics were held and he was placed on BiPap with subsequent improvement. . His hospital course continued with his respiratory status helped some by diuresis. The next morning he was pain free but his bilirubin continued to climb from 2.6 upon admission. Now, his pain has returned in the RUQ though not particularly severe. Bilirubin now 4.5, AlkPhos 185, with a mild transamnitis (60s-80s). GI saw him at ___ and they were unwilling to intervene. Given his persistent pain and transaminitis, RUQ u/s was performed which revealed GB wall inflammation and thickening up to 1cm without any stones visualized. Surg there refused to take him for cholecystectomy, so he was transferred to ___ for potential intervention. . On the floor, he is sedated and difficult to arouse. He is falling asleep during conversation but notes improved abdominal pain. He denies any other symptoms of CP, SOB, palpitations, N, V, diarrhea, constipation, or leg pain. He reports noncompliance with his BiPap machine noting that he "is an idiot". . Review of systems: (+) Per HPI (-) Denies chills, night sweats, recent weight loss or gain. visible_prior_imaging.report:
TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were obtained with a 1.5
Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D images obtained prior to, during and after
the uneventful IV administration of 8 cc of Gadavist. 1 cc of Gadavist mixed
with 50 cc of water was administered orally.

FINDINGS:
The study is limited by motion.  Additional contrast-enhanced sequences could
not be obtained due to the patient's claustrophobia.

The visualized lung bases demonstrates subsegmental atelectasis at the left
lung base. No pericardial or pleural effusion.

The liver demonstrates normal signal intensity on the in and out of phase
images with no evidence of steatosis. There is a 8 x 9 mm T2 hyperintense
lesion in segment 7 which is not well seen on the post-contrast sequence and
may represent a cyst or hemangioma.

There is moderate intrahepatic biliary tree dilatation with irregularity of
the ducts which is predominantly seen centrally and in the left hepatic lobe. 
The common hepatic duct is slightly prominent measuring 10 mm and the common
bile duct measures 9 mm. No obstructing CBD stone identified.  No strictures
seen.  There is mild periportal edema.

The gallbladder demonstrates circumferential wall thickening up to 6 mm
(series 8, image 27) and is distended with a transverse diameter of 5 cm. 
Layering sludge is noted within the gallbladder but no gallstones are
identified.  There is a focal area of T2 hyperintensity in the fundus which
may represent focal adenomyomatosis (series 5, image 36) .

The spleen measures 11.2 cm and is unremarkable. Two 3 mm T2 hyperintense
cystic lesion are noted in the pancreatic body and tail which most likely
represents side-branch IPMNs (series 5, image 27). The pancreas demonstrates
normal signal intensity without any duct dilatation or solid mass.

Bilateral simple cortical renal cysts are noted, the largest one arising from
the upper pole of the left kidney measuring 8 mm (series 5, image 20).

Slightly prominent portocaval lymph node measuring 11 x 15.5 mm. There is a
trace amount of free fluid in the right paracolic gutter.

There is a 11 x 13 mm T2 hyperintense lesion noted in the right hemivertebral
body of L4 most likely in keeping with an hemangioma.

EXAMINATION:
MRI abdomen without and with contrast

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar, multi sequence imaging at 1.5 Tesla. T1 and T2
weighted images, in addition to dynamic in imaging before and after
administration of 9 cc Gadavist IV.

FINDINGS:
This study is moderately limited by patient inability to hold breath, and
respiratory motion artifact.

There appears to be a 2.8 x 1.5 cm hypoenhancing lesion (1103;71, 1104;70-72)
arising from the D1 portions of the duodenum and narrowing its lumen,
represents a previously biopsied neuroendocrine tumor.  
A 3.6 x 2.7 cm T1 hypointense, T2 slightly hyperintense hypoenhancing
lobulated lesion arises along the posterior pancreatic head/uncinate process,
abutting the medial second duodenal segments, immediately posterior to the CBD
and abutting the SMV (1104;71). The inferior aspect of this mass abuts the
second portion of the duodenum, with obscuration of the fat plane and duodenal
wall (series 1103, image 90). The mass abuts the IVC without appreciable
attenuation. 
Another lesion is seen superior to the pancreatic head and anterior to the
common hepatic artery, having a 4.7 x 4.0 cm lobulated component
indistinguishable from adenopathy (1105;63).  The main pancreatic duct within
the head is nonvisualized secondary to mass effect. The main portal vein is
compressed between the lobulated components of the mass/lymphadenopathy and
remains moderately attenuated (series 1103, image 66).

There is no hepatic steatosis.  Three subcentimeter arterially-enhancing foci
within segments ___ and V demonstrate isointensity on other
sequences, representing transient hepatic intensity differences (series 1101,
image 43, 49, 111). Tiny scattered subcentimeter T2 hyperintense lesions
without definite associated enhancement are likely tiny cysts.

A CBD stent is unchanged in position since the prior CT.  Focal proximal CHD
dilation is unchanged (series 7, image 1). No intrahepatic biliary dilatation.

The stomach, intra-abdominal loops of large bowel, spleen, adrenal glands, and
kidneys are normal. An accessory pancreaticoduodenal and/or mesenteric artery
appears to arise directly from the aorta, left of the celiac takeoff (series
1101, image 75). The celiac trunk demonstrates minimal narrowing at the ostium
(series 1101, image 73). Conventional hepatic arterial anatomy is
demonstrated. The renal arteries, SMA, and ___ are patent and normal in
caliber.

Degenerative changes of the spine with probable multilevel Schmorl's nodes and
degenerative endplate changes.

EXAMINATION:
SCROTAL U.S.:

TECHNIQUE:
Grey scale with color and spectral Doppler ultrasound of the
scrotum was performed with linear transducer.

FINDINGS:
The right testicle measures: 4.4 by 2.9 x 1.7 cm.
The left testicle measures:  3.9 x 2.7 x 1.4 cm.

The left testis is heterogeneous weight is multiple nodules that a poorly
marginated. Largest nodule is towards the upper pole and measures 1.7 x 1.2 x
1.9 cm. Nodule at the lower pole measures 0.9 x 0.6 x 1 cm. At least 2 other
tiny nodules also noted. Many of these have an infiltrative appearance. Left
testis also shows increased vascularity spatially at the upper pole.

The right testis echogenicity is normal, without focal abnormalities.
The epididymis is normal bilaterally.
No hydroceles. No varicoceles.

Evaluation of the left groin was also made. Only small normal appearing lymph
nodes identified. No abnormal mass lesion in the groin.

NOTIFICATION:
Critical results dashboard.

visible_prior_imaging.report:
EXAM:
Chest frontal and lateral views.

FINDINGS:
Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  There are
low lung volumes, which accentuate the bronchovascular markings at the lung
bases.  Given this, no focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax
is seen.  Cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are unremarkable.  No evidence
of free air is seen beneath the diaphragms.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images were obtained through the abdomen with the
administration of oral and IV contrast.  Multiplanar reformats were generated
and reviewed.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
The visualized lung bases are clear with no focal
consolidation or pleural effusion.  The visualized heart and pericardium are
unremarkable.  

The liver appears low in attenuation consistent with fatty infiltration with
some areas of fat sparing adjacent to gallbladder fossa.  The gallbladder,
spleen and bilateral adrenal glands appear unremarkable.  Both kidneys enhance
and excrete contrast symmetrically without evidence of hydronephrosis or renal
calculi.

There is swelling of the pancreatic head with slight decrease in attenuation
of the pancreatic head, suggesting edema and extensive stranding surrounding
the pancreas, with inflammatory change and fluid tracking along the second and
third parts of the duodenum, around the porta hepatis and down along the
anterior pararenal space as well as posterior to the ascending colon.  There
is no evidence of free air.  The common bile duct shows mild periductal
enhancement at the level of the head of the pancreas.  No calcified gallstone
is noted.  There is no intrahepatic bile duct dilation.  

The abdominal aorta appears unremarkable.  The portal vein, splenic vein, and
SMV appear patent. An area of soft tissue identical to the prior examination
in the portacaval space measures 20 x 9 mm and is unchanged in size compared
to the most recent prior examination and most likely represents a portacaval
lymph node.  A calcified structure anterior to the esophagus (2:8) is
unchanged from the prior examination may represent a calcified
node.Intra-abdominal loops of large bowel appear grossly unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Four consecutive thoracic vertebral bodies show presence
of Schmorl's nodes.  Slight anterior wedging of L1 and L2 are noted.  Mild
kyphosis is noted. Overall, findings may indicate prior Sc___'s disease.

TECHNIQUE:
Right upper quadrant ultrasound.

FINDINGS:
The liver appears grossly normal without focal liver lesion.  No
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilation is seen.  The CBD measures 5 mm.  The
portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.  The gallbladder contains
multiple shadowing stones; however, appears nondistended without wall
thickening or evidence of pericholecystic fluid.  Limited views of the
pancreas show no focal lesion.  No free fluid is seen.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 1.5
Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior to, during and after
the uneventful intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg (15 mL) of
gadolinium-DTPA.

FINDINGS:
There is marked peripancreatic edema and induration of the peripancreatic fat,
consistent with the patient's clinical diagnosis of ____. The pancreas
appears enlarged and edematous with relatively reduced signal intensity on
pre-contrast T1-weighted images, but enhances homogenously without evidence of
pancreatic necrosis.  The pancreatic duct is not dilated.  Inflammatory
stranding and fluid extends within the mesenteric root, to the paracolic
gutters and along the anterior perirenal fascia bilaterally.   No evidence of
pseudocyst formation. There is edema of the wall of the hepatic flexure,
stomach and duodenum consistent with reactive changes secondary to the upper
abdominal inflammatory process.  The gallbladder is distended, but not thick
walled.  Gallstones seen within the neck of the gallbladder, no
choledocholithiasis.  The common bile duct is not dilated, measuring 4 mm. 
There is loss of signal within the hepatic parenchyma on out-of-phase compared
to in-phase T1-weighted images, consistent with hepatic steatosis.  There is a
poorly defined region of hypoenhancement adjacent to the gallbladder (12:26),
which is unchanged in appearance compared to the CT ___.  This
corresponds to an area of focal fatty change based on the out-of-phase
T1-weighted images (3A:9).  A peripheral segment VI area of hypoenhancement
(12:50) is only seen on one phase post-contrast and is isointense to liver
parenchyma on the remainder of the series.  This likely represents a focal
perfusional abnormality, as no T2 correlate is seen.  No intrahepatic duct
dilatation.  The portal vein and superior mesenteric veins are slightly
narrowed by the peripancreatic/perivascular edema, but patent.  The hepatic
veins are patent.  The hepatic arterial anatomy is conventional.  The splenic
vein is patent.  The spleen is not enlarged.  Both adrenal glands and both
kidneys are unremarkable except to note a cyst in the interpolar region of the
left kidney, measuring 6 mm (13:50).  A tiny cyst noted in the upper pole of
the right kidney.  No upper abdominal lymphadenopathy.   The visualized bone
marrow is unremarkable.

MDCT axial images were acquired from the lung bases through the
lesser trochanters following administration of oral contrast only. 
Subsequently, rapid axial images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
during infusion of 130 cc of intravenous Optiray contrast material. 
Multiplanar reformations were performed.

ABDOMEN CT:
There are new small bilateral pleural effusions.  Minimal
bibasilar atelectasis is greater on the left.  The lung bases are otherwise
clear.

The liver is slightly hypodense, consistent with fat deposition, as seen on
recent MR.  ___ focal liver lesions are identified.  There is ___ intrahepatic
biliary duct dilatation.  The portal vein is patent.  There is high density
fluid/sludge in the gallbladder.  Small gallstones were better demonstrated on
recent MRCP from ___.  There is ___ gallbladder wall thickening
or pericholecystic fluid.  The spleen, adrenal glands, and kidneys are
unremarkable.

As seen on MR from ___, there is marked peripancreatic stranding
with a small quantity of fluid tracking throughout the left anterior pararenal
space and into the pelvis.  The pancreatic head enhances heterogeneously.  
The remainder of the pancreas shows normal enhancement.  The splenic vein
remains patent  There is ___ evidence of a pseudoaneurysm.  The stomach, small
bowel, colon, and appendix are grossly normal.  Small mesenteric and
retroperitoneal lymph nodes do not meet CT size criteria.  The abdominal aorta
is normal in caliber and its main vessels are patent.

PELVIS CT:
The bladder, uterus, and adnexa are unremarkable.  As previously
stated, there is a small quantity of free fluid in the pelvis.  ___
pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph nodes are seen.

BONE WINDOW:
___ suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified.

TECHNIQUE:
Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates diffuse increase in echogenicity. A hypoechoic lesion
measuring 1.8 x 0.9 cm is seen within the right hepatic lobe and likely
represents a region of focal fatty sparing.  There is no evidence of
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The common bile duct
measures 0.4 cm.  The gallbladder is normal and without evidence of stones or
gallbladder wall thickening.  Evaluation of the pancreas is limited by the
patient's body habitus and by adjacent bowel gas, but the visualized portions
appears within normal limits and without evidence of choledocholithiasis or
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  The right kidney measures 11.4 cm, and is
without evidence of hydronephrosis or solid renal mass. There is no ascites.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
The lung volumes are low.  Bilateral pleural effusions, better seen
on the lateral than on the frontal radiograph.  Subsequent areas of mild
atelectasis at the lung bases.  Borderline size of the cardiac silhouette
without evidence of fluid overload.
